tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SearchPlugins
tools.description:
Search the user's claude.ai plugin catalog by keyword. Call this when a plugin (slash command, skill bundle, hook, or agent) from the user's org catalog might help complete the task. The user does not need to name a plugin: search when the task depends on their team's own process, systems or data and nothing you already have, the project's own scripts included, covers it.

Examples:
- "use the deploy plugin" → keywords ["deploy"]
- "is there something for linting?" → keywords ["lint", "format", "code quality"]
- "ship this to staging" → keywords ["deploy", "release", "staging"]
- "review this contract against our playbook" → keywords ["legal", "contract", "playbook"]
- "which deals close this week?" → keywords ["sales", "pipeline", "crm"]

Do not search unasked for one-off questions or tasks you can handle directly ("explain this regex", "fix this typo"), or after the user ignored a suggestion in this conversation.

Returns a ranked list with id, name, description, and whether the plugin is already enabled for this session (in a channel session, whether the channel has it). When results fit and SuggestPluginInstall is among your tools, call it to render the install card; otherwise relay the relevant results in text instead. If nothing relevant, proceed without mentioning that you searched.

tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields (write recap last) — ask and recap are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available, or one your own work this turn made available; others are refused, and one that later stops being available is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and other answers), so do not guess. label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Not now": a button, not a sentence. A click sends it to you as the user's answer. Never a go-ahead to commit: that is the commit app action. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action.

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments. Never repeat an offer the user passed over, as an app action, a reply or a question in your closing message, unless what it acts on has changed since or they bring it up.

Its first sentence is the sidebar status. tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

attachment.cliPrefix: You are Claude Code, Anthropic's official CLI for Claude, running within the Claude Agent SDK.

lastPrompt: First note that if the announcement states that Y will assume the role on a future date, X should not automatically become Former on the day the announcement is published. The effective date of the ap…

content.content:
1	"""Decide which roles are current, former or unverified. SPEC section 3.6.
2	
3	`resolve` is a pure function: claims and a date in, roles out. It reads no
4	clock, database or network, and never asks a model. Every status it returns
5	names the rule that produced it.
6	
7	Principles
8	- Concurrent roles are normal; a different title elsewhere is not a conflict.
9	- A role ends only on evidence. Age alone can only downgrade to unverified.
10	- Explicit events (appointments, departures) outrank page listings.
11	- Reliability outranks recency: a lower tier never overrides a higher one.
12	- Leaving a role is not leaving the company.
13	"""
14	
15	from __future__ import annotations
16	
17	import calendar
18	import re
19	from collections import defaultdict
20	from collections.abc import Iterable
21	from dataclasses import dataclass
22	from datetime import date
23	
24	CURRENT, FORMER, UNVERIFIED = "current", "former", "unverified"
25	
26	# status_reason values, one per rule.
27	R1_END = "rule1_explicit_end"
28	R1_FUTURE = "rule1_departure_announced_for_future_date"
29	R2_REPORTED = "rule2_departure_reported_by_news_only"
30	R3_APPOINTED = "rule3_successor_appointed"
31	R3_LISTED = "rule3_successor_listed_on_company_page"
32	R4_LISTED = "rule4_listed_on_company_page"
33	R5_SUPPORTED = "rule5_recent_reliable_source"
34	R6_WEAK = "rule6_stale_or_weak_evidence"
35	R7_OUTRANKED = "rule7_outranked_in_single_holder_role"
36	
37	
38	@dataclass(frozen=True)
39	class Claim:
40	    """One observation, joined with the tier and type of its source."""
41	
42	    id: int
43	    person_id: int
44	    source_id: int
45	    claim_type: str                 # role | appointment | departure | location | bio
46	    tier: int                       # 1 (best) to 4, from the source
47	    source_type: str
48	    as_of_date: date                # published date, or retrieval date for live pages
49	    as_of_basis: str                # published | retrieved
50	    effective_date: date | None = None
51	    raw_title: str | None = None
52	    level: str | None = None
53	    department: str | None = None
54	    canonical_role: str | None = None   # set only for single-holder roles (CEO, CFO, ...)
55	    departure_scope: str | None = None  # role | company
56	
57	    @property
58	    def when(self) -> date:
59	        """When the fact took effect: the stated date, else the source's date."""
60	        return self.effective_date or self.as_of_date
61	
62	    @property
63	    def is_live_listing(self) -> bool:
64	        """A role shown on the company's own site as retrieved now."""
65	        return (self.claim_type == "role" and self.tier == 1
66	                and self.source_type == "company_site" and self.as_of_basis == "retrieved")
67	
68	    @property
69	    def is_dated(self) -> bool:
70	        """Has a real date. An undated article only has its retrieval date: weak."""
71	        return self.effective_date is not None or self.as_of_basis == "published"
72	
73	
74	@dataclass
75	class Role:
76	    person_id: int
77	    key: str
78	    title: str
79	    level: str | None
80	    department: str | None
81	    canonical_role: str | None
82	    status: str
83	    status_reason: str
84	    ended_on: date | None = None
85	    ended_by_claim_id: int | None = None
86	    first_seen: date | None = None
87	    last_seen: date | None = None
88	    conflict: bool = False
89	    conflict_reason: str | None = None
90	    conflicting_claim_id: int | None = None
91	    source_count: int = 0
92	    supporting_claim_id: int | None = None
93	
94	
95	@dataclass
96	class Resolution:
97	    roles: list[Role]
98	    employment: dict[int, str]      # person_id -> current | former | unknown
99	
100	
101	def role_key(c: Claim) -> str | None:
102	    """What counts as 'the same role' for one person across sources."""
103	    if c.canonical_role:
104	        return c.canonical_role
105	    if c.level in ("c_level", "vp", "head") and c.department and c.department != "other":
106	        return f"{c.level}:{c.department}"
107	    if c.raw_title:
108	        return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", " ", c.raw_title.casefold()).strip() or None
109	    return None
110	
111	
112	def _months_before(d: date, months: int) -> date:
113	    y, m = divmod(d.year * 12 + d.month - 1 - months, 12)
114	    return date(y, m + 1, min(d.day, calendar.monthrange(y, m + 1)[1]))
115	
116	
117	def _best(claims: list[Claim]) -> Claim:
118	    """Most reliable, then most recent, then lowest id (for determinism)."""
119	    return min(claims, key=lambda c: (c.tier, -c.when.toordinal(), c.id))
120	
121	
122	def resolve(claims: Iterable[Claim], today: date, freshness_months: int = 12) -> Resolution:
123	    claims = sorted(claims, key=lambda c: c.id)     # order of input must not matter
124	    cutoff = _months_before(today, freshness_months)
125	
126	    support: dict[tuple[int, str], list[Claim]] = defaultdict(list)
127	    departures: dict[int, list[Claim]] = defaultdict(list)
128	    for c in claims:
129	        key = role_key(c)
130	        if c.claim_type in ("role", "appointment") and key:
131	            if c.claim_type == "appointment" and c.when > today:
132	                continue                            # not in the role yet
133	            support[(c.person_id, key)].append(c)
134	        elif c.claim_type == "departure" and c.tier <= 3:   # snippets alone change nothing
135	            departures[c.person_id].append(c)
136	            if c.departure_scope == "role" and key:
137	                support.setdefault((c.person_id, key), [])  # role known only from its end
138	
139	    # Indexes for single-holder roles.
140	    live_by_role: dict[str, list[Claim]] = defaultdict(list)
141	    appointed_by_role: dict[str, list[Claim]] = defaultdict(list)
142	    for c in claims:
143	        if not c.canonical_role:
144	            continue
145	        if c.is_live_listing:
146	            live_by_role[c.canonical_role].append(c)
147	        elif c.claim_type == "appointment" and c.tier <= 2 and c.when <= today:
148	            appointed_by_role[c.canonical_role].append(c)
149	
150	    def is_fresh(c: Claim) -> bool:
151	        return c.tier <= 3 and c.is_dated and c.when >= cutoff
152	
153	    def successor(pid: int, canonical: str | None, sup: list[Claim]) -> tuple[Claim, str] | None:
154	        if not canonical:
155	            return None
156	        listed = any(s.is_live_listing for s in sup)
157	        dated = [s.when for s in sup if s.is_dated and not s.is_live_listing]
158	        latest = max(dated, default=None)
159	        live_holders = {c.person_id for c in live_by_role[canonical]}

"""Check that the worked cases can actually fail.

    uv run python tools/mutation_check.py

Passing tests prove little if they would also pass with a broken rule. This
script breaks the resolution rules one at a time, in memory only (the file on
disk is never changed), and re-runs every worked case against the broken
version. Each break must make at least one case fail.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import dataclasses
import sys
import types
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
sys.path[:0] = [str(ROOT), str(ROOT / "tests")]

from worked_cases import CASES, TODAY  # noqa: E402

SOURCE = (ROOT / "leadership" / "resolve.py").read_text(encoding="utf-8")

# (what is broken, exact text in resolve.py, replacement)
MUTATIONS = [
    ("A news-only departure ends the role (rule 2 removed)",
     "strong = [d for d in deps if d.tier <= 2]",
     "strong = [d for d in deps if d.tier <= 3]"),
    ("Old documents count as fresh (freshness window removed)",
     "return c.tier <= 3 and c.is_dated and c.when >= cutoff",
     "return c.tier <= 3 and c.is_dated"),
    ("Undated articles count as dated",
     "return self.effective_date is not None or self.as_of_basis == \"published\"",
     "return True"),
    ("Leaving the company no longer ends the person's roles",
     "(d.departure_scope == \"company\" or role_key(d) == key)",
     "(role_key(d) == key)"),
    ("Single-holder conflicts are not detected (rule 7 removed)",
     "if len({r.person_id for r in group}) < 2:",
     "if True:"),
    ("An appointment ends a co-holder shown on the same page",
     "if listed and a.person_id in live_holders:",
     "if False:"),
    ("Succession is never detected (rule 3 removed)",
     "elif (succ := successor(pid, canonical, sup)):",
     "elif (succ := None):"),
    ("A live page listing no longer makes a role current (rule 4 removed)",
     "elif listed:                                                # rule 4",
     "elif False:"),
    ("A future departure date is treated as already past",
     "if d.when <= today:\n                role.status, role.status_reason = FORMER, R1_END",
     "if True:\n                role.status, role.status_reason = FORMER, R1_END"),
    ("A search snippet can report a departure",
     "elif c.claim_type == \"departure\" and c.tier <= 3:",
     "elif c.claim_type == \"departure\" and c.tier <= 4:"),
    ("A later re-appointment no longer cancels an earlier departure",
     "and not any(a.claim_type == \"appointment\" and a.when > d.when for a in sup)",
     ""),
]


def failing_cases(source: str) -> int:
    module = types.ModuleType("mutated_resolve")
    sys.modules[module.__name__] = module       # dataclasses look the module up by name
    exec(compile(source, "mutated_resolve.py", "exec"), module.__dict__)
    failed = 0
    for case in CASES:
        try:
            # Rebuild each claim with the mutated Claim class, so that breaks
            # inside Claim's own properties take effect too.
            claims = [module.Claim(**dataclasses.asdict(c)) for c in case["claims"]]
            result = module.resolve(claims, case.get("today", TODAY))
            got = {(r.person_id, r.key): (r.status, r.status_reason) for r in result.roles}
            ok = got == case["expect"] and result.employment == case["employment"]
        except Exception:
            ok = False
        failed += not ok
    return failed


def main() -> int:
    baseline = failing_cases(SOURCE)
    print(f"Unmodified rules: {baseline} of {len(CASES)} cases fail (must be 0)")
    survived = 0
    for name, old, new in MUTATIONS:
        if SOURCE.count(old) != 1:
            print(f"  NOT APPLIED  {name}  (text not found exactly once)")
            survived += 1
            continue
        failed = failing_cases(SOURCE.replace(old, new))
        survived += failed == 0
        print(f"  {'caught  ' if failed else 'SURVIVED'}  {name}  ->  {failed} case(s) fail")
    print(f"\n{len(MUTATIONS) - survived} of {len(MUTATIONS)} broken rules were caught by the worked cases")
    return 1 if baseline or survived else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""Worked cases for role resolution (SPEC section 3.6).

Each case is a small set of claims and the outcome the rules must produce.
The same list drives the unit tests and `tools/show_cases.py`, which prints
it as a table for manual review.
"""

from datetime import date

from leadership.resolve import (CURRENT, FORMER, R1_END, R1_FUTURE, R2_REPORTED,
                                R3_APPOINTED, R3_LISTED, R4_LISTED, R5_SUPPORTED,
                                R6_WEAK, R7_OUTRANKED, UNVERIFIED, Claim)

TODAY = date(2026, 11, 1)
X, Y = 1, 2     # two people


def _c(id, person, kind, title=None, *, tier, src, on, basis="published", eff=None,
       canonical=None, level="c_level", dept="other", scope=None, source=None):
    return Claim(id=id, person_id=person, source_id=source or id, claim_type=kind,
                 tier=tier, source_type=src, as_of_date=on, as_of_basis=basis,
                 effective_date=eff, raw_title=title, level=level, department=dept,
                 canonical_role=canonical, departure_scope=scope)


def live(id, person, title, **kw):          # company's own leadership page, retrieved today
    return _c(id, person, "role", title, tier=1, src="company_site", on=TODAY, basis="retrieved", **kw)


def filing(id, person, title, on, **kw):    # SEC filing
    return _c(id, person, "role", title, tier=1, src="sec_filing", on=on, **kw)


def release(id, person, title, on, **kw):   # press release on the company's site
    return _c(id, person, "role", title, tier=2, src="press_release", on=on, **kw)


def news(id, person, title, on, **kw):      # third-party article
    return _c(id, person, "role", title, tier=3, src="news", on=on, **kw)


def snippet(id, person, title, **kw):       # search-result snippet
    return _c(id, person, "role", title, tier=4, src="search_snippet", on=TODAY, basis="retrieved", **kw)


def departure(id, person, scope, *, tier, src, on, **kw):
    return _c(id, person, "departure", kw.pop("title", None), tier=tier, src=src, on=on, scope=scope, **kw)


def appointment(id, person, title, *, tier, src, on, **kw):
    return _c(id, person, "appointment", title, tier=tier, src=src, on=on, **kw)


CTO = dict(canonical="CTO")
CFO = dict(canonical="CFO")
CEO = dict(canonical="CEO")

# expect: {(person, role key): (status, rule)}    employment: {person: status}
CASES = [
    dict(
        name="Only an old press release names X as CTO",
        claims=[release(1, X, "CTO", date(2023, 5, 1), **CTO)],
        expect={(X, "CTO"): (UNVERIFIED, R6_WEAK)},
        employment={X: "unknown"},
    ),
    dict(
        name="Live leadership page lists X",
        claims=[live(1, X, "CTO", **CTO)],
        expect={(X, "CTO"): (CURRENT, R4_LISTED)},
        employment={X: "current"},
    ),
    dict(
        name="Page lists X; a company release says X stepped down as CTO",
        claims=[live(1, X, "CTO", **CTO),
                departure(2, X, "role", tier=2, src="press_release", on=date(2026, 9, 15), title="CTO", **CTO)],
        expect={(X, "CTO"): (FORMER, R1_END)},
        employment={X: "unknown"},
    ),
    dict(
        name="Page lists X; an SEC filing says X left the company",
        claims=[live(1, X, "CTO", **CTO),
                departure(2, X, "company", tier=1, src="sec_filing", on=date(2026, 9, 15))],
        expect={(X, "CTO"): (FORMER, R1_END)},
        employment={X: "former"},
    ),
    dict(
        name="Page lists X; only a news article reports the departure",
        claims=[live(1, X, "CTO", **CTO),
                departure(2, X, "role", tier=3, src="news", on=date(2026, 10, 1), title="CTO", **CTO)],
        expect={(X, "CTO"): (UNVERIFIED, R2_REPORTED)},
        employment={X: "unknown"},
    ),
    dict(
        name="No page lists X; only a news article reports the departure",
        claims=[release(1, X, "CTO", date(2026, 3, 1), **CTO),
                departure(2, X, "role", tier=3, src="news", on=date(2026, 9, 1), title="CTO", **CTO)],
        expect={(X, "CTO"): (UNVERIFIED, R2_REPORTED)},
        employment={X: "unknown"},
    ),
    dict(
        name="Departure announced with a future effective date",
        claims=[live(1, X, "CTO", **CTO),
                departure(2, X, "role", tier=2, src="press_release", on=date(2026, 10, 20),
                          eff=date(2026, 12, 31), title="CTO", **CTO)],
        expect={(X, "CTO"): (CURRENT, R1_FUTURE)},
        employment={X: "current"},
    ),
    dict(
        name="Old release names X; live page shows Y in that role",
        claims=[release(1, X, "CTO", date(2023, 5, 1), **CTO), live(2, Y, "CTO", **CTO)],
        expect={(X, "CTO"): (FORMER, R3_LISTED), (Y, "CTO"): (CURRENT, R4_LISTED)},
        employment={X: "unknown", Y: "current"},
    ),
    dict(
        name="X steps down as CTO, stays as board advisor",
        claims=[release(1, X, "CTO", date(2025, 2, 1), **CTO),
                departure(2, X, "role", tier=2, src="press_release", on=date(2026, 8, 1), title="CTO", **CTO),
                live(3, X, "Board Advisor", level="other")],
        expect={(X, "CTO"): (FORMER, R1_END), (X, "board advisor"): (CURRENT, R4_LISTED)},
        employment={X: "current"},
    ),
    dict(
        name="X's only role ends; nothing says X left the company",
        claims=[release(1, X, "CTO", date(2025, 2, 1), **CTO),
                departure(2, X, "role", tier=2, src="press_release", on=date(2026, 8, 1), title="CTO", **CTO)],
        expect={(X, "CTO"): (FORMER, R1_END)},
        employment={X: "unknown"},
    ),
    dict(
        name="Concurrent roles: X is CEO on the page and Chair in a filing",
        claims=[live(1, X, "Co-founder and CEO", **CEO),
                filing(2, X, "Chair of the Board", date(2026, 4, 1), level="other")],
        expect={(X, "CEO"): (CURRENT, R4_LISTED),
                (X, "chair of the board"): (CURRENT, R5_SUPPORTED)},
        employment={X: "current"},
    ),
    dict(
        name="Successor appointed: Y becomes CFO; X keeps another role",
        claims=[filing(1, X, "CFO", date(2026, 2, 1), source=10, **CFO),
                filing(2, X, "President", date(2026, 2, 1), source=10),
                appointment(3, Y, "CFO", tier=2, src="press_release", on=date(2026, 7, 15),
                            eff=date(2026, 8, 1), **CFO)],
        expect={(X, "CFO"): (FORMER, R3_APPOINTED), (X, "president"): (CURRENT, R5_SUPPORTED),
                (Y, "CFO"): (CURRENT, R5_SUPPORTED)},
        employment={X: "current", Y: "current"},
    ),
    dict(
        name="Company release appoints Y as CTO; the page still lists only X (page lags)",
        claims=[live(1, X, "CTO", **CTO),
                appointment(2, Y, "CTO", tier=2, src="press_release", on=date(2026, 9, 1), **CTO)],

309-`tests/worked_cases.py`):
310-
311-- *Same role.* For one person, two claims describe the same role when they
312-  share a canonical role (CEO, CFO, ...); otherwise the same level and
313-  department; otherwise the same normalized title.
314-- *Rule 3, appointment.* An appointment of Y does not end X's role when the
315-  live page lists both (co-holders), or when X has a dated source later than
316-  the appointment. Those cases go to rule 7 as a conflict.
317-- *Rule 3, listing.* "The page shows someone else" ends X's role only when X
318-  is not on the page and has no recent reliable source. If X does have one,
319-  both stay and rule 7 flags the conflict.
320-- *Rule 5.* It is enough that any supporting claim is tier 1–3, dated, and
321-  within the window; a newer snippet does not cancel it.
322-- *Returns.* A later appointment to a role cancels an earlier departure.
323-- *Future appointments* are not roles until their effective date.
324-- *Roles known only from their end* ("former CTO X" in a company release) are
325-  recorded as `former`, so history questions can be answered. A snippet alone
326-  is too weak to record anything.

328-Each role stores `status_reason` (the rule that decided it), the claim that

330-independent sources supporting it. A role flagged as a conflict also stores

1	"""Check that the worked cases can actually fail.
2	
3	    uv run python tools/mutation_check.py
4	
5	Passing tests prove little if they would also pass with a broken rule. This
6	script breaks the resolution rules one at a time, in memory only (the file on
7	disk is never changed), and re-runs every worked case against the broken
8	version. Each break must make at least one case fail.
9	"""
10	
11	from __future__ import annotations
12	
13	import dataclasses
14	import sys
15	import types
16	from pathlib import Path
17	
18	ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
19	sys.path[:0] = [str(ROOT), str(ROOT / "tests")]
20	
21	from worked_cases import CASES, TODAY  # noqa: E402
22	
23	SOURCE = (ROOT / "leadership" / "resolve.py").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
24	
25	# (what is broken, exact text in resolve.py, replacement)
26	MUTATIONS = [
27	    ("A news-only departure ends the role (rule 2 removed)",
28	     "strong = [d for d in deps if d.tier <= 2]",
29	     "strong = [d for d in deps if d.tier <= 3]"),
30	    ("Old documents count as fresh (freshness window removed)",
31	     "return c.tier <= 3 and c.is_dated and c.when >= cutoff",
32	     "return c.tier <= 3 and c.is_dated"),
33	    ("Undated articles count as dated",
34	     "return self.effective_date is not None or self.as_of_basis == \"published\"",
35	     "return True"),
36	    ("Leaving the company no longer ends the person's roles",
37	     "(d.departure_scope == \"company\" or role_key(d) == key)",
38	     "(role_key(d) == key)"),
39	    ("Single-holder conflicts are not detected (rule 7 removed)",
40	     "if len({r.person_id for r in group}) < 2:",
41	     "if True:"),
42	    ("An appointment ends a co-holder shown on the same page",
43	     "if listed and a.person_id in live_holders:",
44	     "if False:"),
45	    ("Succession is never detected (rule 3 removed)",
46	     "elif (succ := successor(pid, canonical, sup)):",
47	     "elif (succ := None):"),
48	    ("A live page listing no longer makes a role current (rule 4 removed)",
49	     "elif listed:                                                # rule 4",
50	     "elif False:"),
51	    ("A future departure date is treated as already past",
52	     "if d.when <= today:\n                role.status, role.status_reason = FORMER, R1_END",
53	     "if True:\n                role.status, role.status_reason = FORMER, R1_END"),
54	    ("A search snippet can report a departure",
55	     "elif c.claim_type == \"departure\" and c.tier <= 3:",
56	     "elif c.claim_type == \"departure\" and c.tier <= 4:"),
57	    ("A later re-appointment no longer cancels an earlier departure",
58	     "and not any(a.claim_type == \"appointment\" and a.when > d.when for a in sup)",
59	     ""),
60	]
61	
62	
63	def failing_cases(source: str) -> int:
64	    module = types.ModuleType("mutated_resolve")
65	    sys.modules[module.__name__] = module       # dataclasses look the module up by name
66	    exec(compile(source, "mutated_resolve.py", "exec"), module.__dict__)
67	    failed = 0
68	    for case in CASES:
69	        try:
70	            # Rebuild each claim with the mutated Claim class, so that breaks
71	            # inside Claim's own properties take effect too.
72	            claims = [module.Claim(**dataclasses.asdict(c)) for c in case["claims"]]
73	            result = module.resolve(claims, case.get("today", TODAY))
74	            got = {(r.person_id, r.key): (r.status, r.status_reason) for r in result.roles}
75	            ok = got == case["expect"] and result.employment == case["employment"]
76	        except Exception:
77	            ok = False
78	        failed += not ok
79	    return failed
80	
81	
82	def main() -> int:
83	    baseline = failing_cases(SOURCE)
84	    print(f"Unmodified rules: {baseline} of {len(CASES)} cases fail (must be 0)")
85	    survived = 0
86	    for name, old, new in MUTATIONS:
87	        if SOURCE.count(old) != 1:
88	            print(f"  NOT APPLIED  {name}  (text not found exactly once)")
89	            survived += 1
90	            continue
91	        failed = failing_cases(SOURCE.replace(old, new))
92	        survived += failed == 0
93	        print(f"  {'caught  ' if failed else 'SURVIVED'}  {name}  ->  {failed} case(s) fail")
94	    print(f"\n{len(MUTATIONS) - survived} of {len(MUTATIONS)} broken rules were caught by the worked cases")
95	    return 1 if baseline or survived else 0
96	
97	
98	if __name__ == "__main__":
99	    sys.exit(main())

313-  department; otherwise the same normalized title.

315-  live page lists both (co-holders), or when X has a dated source later than
316-  the appointment. Those cases go to rule 7 as a conflict.

318-  is not on the page and has no recent reliable source. If X does have one,
319-  both stay and rule 7 flags the conflict.
320-- *Rule 5.* It is enough that any supporting claim is tier 1–3, dated, and
321-  within the window; a newer snippet does not cancel it.

"""Check that the worked cases can actually fail.

Passing tests prove little if they would also pass with a broken rule. This
script breaks the resolution rules one at a time, in memory only (the file on
disk is never changed), and re-runs every worked case against the broken
version. Each break must make at least one case fail.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import dataclasses
import sys
import types
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
sys.path[:0] = [str(ROOT), str(ROOT / "tests")]

from worked_cases import CASES, TODAY  # noqa: E402

def failing_cases(source: str) -> int:
    module = types.ModuleType("mutated_resolve")
    sys.modules[module.__name__] = module       # dataclasses look the module up by name
    exec(compile(source, "mutated_resolve.py", "exec"), module.__dict__)
    failed = 0
    for case in CASES:
        try:
            # Rebuild each claim with the mutated Claim class, so that breaks
            # inside Claim's own properties take effect too.
            claims = [module.Claim(**dataclasses.asdict(c)) for c in case["claims"]]
            result = module.resolve(claims, case.get("today", TODAY))
            got = {(r.person_id, r.key): (r.status, r.status_reason) for r in result.roles}
            ok = got == case["expect"] and result.employment == case["employment"]
        except Exception:
            ok = False
        failed += not ok
    return failed


def main() -> int:
    baseline = failing_cases(SOURCE)
    print(f"Unmodified rules: {baseline} of {len(CASES)} cases fail (must be 0)")
    survived = 0
    for name, old, new in MUTATIONS:
        if SOURCE.count(old) != 1:
            print(f"  NOT APPLIED  {name}  (text not found exactly once)")
            survived += 1
            continue
        failed = failing_cases(SOURCE.replace(old, new))
        survived += failed == 0
        print(f"  {'caught  ' if failed else 'SURVIVED'}  {name}  ->  {failed} case(s) fail")
    print(f"\n{len(MUTATIONS) - survived} of {len(MUTATIONS)} broken rules were caught by the worked cases")
    return 1 if baseline or survived else 0

content.text:
Yes, that is right, and the rules already behaved that way: an appointment with a future effective date is ignored until that date, so it neither gives Y the role nor ends X's. What was missing was a worked case proving the X side, so I added it.

- **Case 29:** a release in October says Y becomes CFO on 1 January; X is the CFO in a filing. Viewed on 1 November, X is `current` and Y holds nothing yet.
- **Case 30:** the same claims viewed on 2 January. X is `former` with the end date 1 January, and Y is `current`.
- **Mutation check:** a new break, "a future appointment ends the holder's role on the day it is announced", is caught by case 29.

M1 acceptance re-ran with 6 of 6 steps as expected: 77 fast tests passed, 30 of 30 cases match, 12 of 12 broken rules caught. The rule is written out in SPEC section 3.6, the counts in `acceptance/M1.md` are updated, and the checklist has a new row R136 (136 requirements, no formula errors). Nothing is committed yet.

One gap remains. The rule only works if the effective date is captured during extraction, which is M3. A claim with no effective date is dated by its publication date, so an announcement that says "will become CFO" without naming a date would make X `former` on the day it is published. My recommendation is that such an announcement should not end X's role until a dated source confirms it.

Until you run the M1 manual tests, two side effects of the current behaviour are worth knowing:
- **Y is invisible before the effective date.** The chat cannot answer "who will be the next CFO?" because the future appointment produces no role row.
- **X shows no warning.** X is plain `current` with no note that a successor has been announced.

content: That makes sense, and I agree with the new cases. I think we should also fix the remaining issues before finishing M1. If an announcement says someone "will become CFO" but doesn't give a date, we shouldn't assume the change happens on the publication date. The current CFO should stay current until there's evidence the transition has happened. I'd also like to keep future appointments in the data, so users can still ask who the next CFO will be, without counting that person as a current executive. And if a successor has already been announced, it would be useful to show that next to the current executive's role. Can you suggest a simple way to handle these without making the system too complicated? I'd like to review the approach before you make changes.

Yes. All three can be handled with one small flag on claims, one new role status, and one link on roles, and the seven rules stay in the same order.

## 1. "Will become CFO" with no date

- **Change:** claims get one new field, `effective_pending`, which extraction sets when the source describes the change as future and gives no date.
- **Behaviour:** a pending appointment has no effect on its own, so X stays `current`.
- **What counts as evidence the transition happened:** a later source that shows Y in the role. That is the live page listing Y, a dated tier 1–3 source published after the announcement naming Y in the role, or a later past-tense appointment.
- **Then:** the appointment takes effect on the date of that evidence, and the existing rule 3 ends X's role as it does today.

I would apply the same flag to departures ("X will step down", no date), because rule 1 has the same problem: it would end the role on the publication date.

## 2. Keeping future appointments visible

- **Change:** a fourth role status, `announced`, with a `starts_on` date that is empty when no date was given.
- **Behaviour:** Y gets a role row with status `announced` instead of no row at all.
- **Not counted as current:** the `current_leadership` view only includes `current`, so "How many C-level executives?" is unaffected. The `leadership` view includes the row, so "Who will be the next CFO?" can be answered with its source.
- **Employment:** Y's employment stays `unknown` unless Y holds another current role, since Y may be an outside hire.

## 3. Successor shown next to the current executive

- **Change:** roles get `successor_claim_id`, pointing at the announcement.
- **Behaviour:** X's row stays `current` with no conflict flag. The view adds the successor's name, start date and source, so the chat can say "X is CFO; Y has been announced as successor from 1 January (source)".

## Outcomes

| Situation | X | Y |
|---|---|---|
| Announced with a future date, before it | `current`, successor shown | `announced`, starts on that date |
| Same, after the date | `former` | `current` |
| Announced with no date, nothing else | `current`, successor shown | `announced`, no start date |
| No date, then the page lists Y | `former` | `current` |

## Defaults I would pick

- **Source tier:** announcements from tier 1–3 sources are shown; search snippets are ignored. The successor note is informational and never changes X's status.
- **Stale announcements:** an undated announcement older than the 12-month window with no confirmation becomes `unverified`.
- **Reason codes:** `announced` rows get their own status reason, so every role still names the rule that decided it.

## Cost

- **Schema:** one claim column, two role columns, one extra status value, three view columns.
- **Rules:** one step before rule 1 that sorts appointments into effective, pending and announced.
- **Tests:** about six new worked cases and two or three new mutations.
- **M3:** the extraction prompt must report whether a change is past or future, in addition to the effective date.

Tell me if you want any of the defaults changed; otherwise I'll build it this way and re-run the M1 acceptance.

"""SQLite schema and the bridge between stored claims and derived roles.

Claims are append-only observations. Roles and employment status are derived:
`rebuild_roles` deletes and recomputes them from claims with the pure function
`resolve.resolve`, so they can be regenerated at any time. See SPEC section 4.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import sqlite3
from datetime import date
from pathlib import Path

from .resolve import Claim, resolve

SCHEMA = """
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS companies (
    id            INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    domain        TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    name          TEXT NOT NULL,
    collected_at  TEXT
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS runs (
    id           INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    company_id   INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES companies(id),
    started_at   TEXT NOT NULL,
    finished_at  TEXT,
    status       TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'running' CHECK (status IN
                 ('running','complete','budget_exhausted','insufficient_data',
                  'partial_failure','interrupted')),
    reasons      TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]',   -- JSON list: every condition that applied
    counters     TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'    -- JSON: usage against each limit
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS sources (
    id            INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    company_id    INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES companies(id),
    url           TEXT NOT NULL,
    source_type   TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (source_type IN
                  ('company_site','sec_filing','press_release','news','wikipedia','search_snippet')),
    tier          INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (tier BETWEEN 1 AND 4),
    title         TEXT,
    published_at  TEXT,                         -- NULL when unknown; never guessed
    retrieved_at  TEXT NOT NULL,
    content_hash  TEXT,
    stage         TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'fetched' CHECK (stage IN
                  ('fetched','extracted','failed','skipped')),
    attempts      INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    last_error    TEXT,
    UNIQUE (company_id, url)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS people (
    id                 INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    company_id         INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES companies(id),
    full_name          TEXT NOT NULL,
    normalized_name    TEXT NOT NULL,
    linkedin_url       TEXT,
    employment_status  TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'unknown' CHECK (employment_status IN
                       ('current','former','unknown'))      -- DERIVED
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS claims (
    id                  INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    company_id          INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES companies(id),
    person_id           INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES people(id),
    source_id           INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES sources(id),
    claim_type          TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (claim_type IN
                        ('role','appointment','departure','location','bio')),
    departure_scope     TEXT CHECK (departure_scope IN ('role','company')),
    raw_title           TEXT,
    level               TEXT CHECK (level IN ('c_level','vp','head','other')),
    department          TEXT,
    canonical_role      TEXT,
    value               TEXT,                   -- location / bio text
    evidence            TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(trim(evidence)) > 0),
    as_of_date          TEXT NOT NULL,          -- ISO date
    as_of_basis         TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (as_of_basis IN ('published','retrieved')),
    effective_date      TEXT,                   -- stated in the text, if any
    extraction_version  TEXT NOT NULL,
    CHECK (claim_type <> 'departure' OR departure_scope IS NOT NULL)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS roles (                -- DERIVED, rebuilt by rebuild_roles
    id                    INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    company_id            INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES companies(id),
    person_id             INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES people(id),
    title                 TEXT NOT NULL,
    level                 TEXT,
    department            TEXT,
    canonical_role        TEXT,
    status                TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('current','former','unverified')),
    status_reason         TEXT NOT NULL,        -- the rule in SPEC 3.6 that decided
    ended_on              TEXT,
    ended_by_claim_id     INTEGER REFERENCES claims(id),   -- departure or successor evidence
    first_seen            TEXT,
    last_seen             TEXT,
    last_verified_at      TEXT,
    conflict              INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    conflict_reason       TEXT,
    conflicting_claim_id  INTEGER REFERENCES claims(id),   -- evidence on the other side
    source_count          INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    supporting_claim_id   INTEGER REFERENCES claims(id)
);

-- The two views below are the only objects the chat agent may read.
CREATE VIEW IF NOT EXISTS leadership AS
SELECT
    c.domain               AS company_domain,
    c.name                 AS company,
    p.full_name            AS person,
    p.employment_status    AS employment_status,
    r.title, r.level, r.department, r.canonical_role,
    r.status, r.status_reason, r.ended_on,
    r.first_seen, r.last_seen, r.last_verified_at,
    r.conflict, r.conflict_reason, r.source_count,
    (SELECT l.value FROM claims l JOIN sources ls ON ls.id = l.source_id
      WHERE l.person_id = p.id AND l.claim_type = 'location'
      ORDER BY ls.tier, l.as_of_date DESC, l.id LIMIT 1)        AS location,
    (SELECT ls.url FROM claims l JOIN sources ls ON ls.id = l.source_id
      WHERE l.person_id = p.id AND l.claim_type = 'location'
      ORDER BY ls.tier, l.as_of_date DESC, l.id LIMIT 1)        AS location_source_url,
    (SELECT l.value FROM claims l JOIN sources ls ON ls.id = l.source_id
      WHERE l.person_id = p.id AND l.claim_type = 'bio'
      ORDER BY ls.tier, l.as_of_date DESC, l.id LIMIT 1)        AS bio,
    s.url                  AS source_url,
    s.source_type          AS source_type,
    sc.as_of_date          AS source_date,
    substr(sc.evidence, 1, 300) AS evidence,
    cs.url                 AS conflicting_source_url,
    substr(cc.evidence, 1, 300) AS conflicting_evidence
FROM roles r
JOIN people p     ON p.id = r.person_id
JOIN companies c  ON c.id = r.company_id
LEFT JOIN claims sc  ON sc.id = r.supporting_claim_id
LEFT JOIN sources s  ON s.id = sc.source_id
LEFT JOIN claims cc  ON cc.id = r.conflicting_claim_id
LEFT JOIN sources cs ON cs.id = cc.source_id;

CREATE VIEW IF NOT EXISTS current_leadership AS
SELECT * FROM leadership
WHERE status = 'current' AND level IN ('c_level', 'vp', 'head');
"""


def connect(path: str | Path) -> sqlite3.Connection:
    """Open (and create if needed) the database with the schema applied."""
    conn = sqlite3.connect(str(path))
    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    conn.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON")
    conn.executescript(SCHEMA)
    return conn


def load_claims(conn: sqlite3.Connection, company_id: int) -> list[Claim]:
    rows = conn.execute(
        """SELECT cl.*, s.tier, s.source_type
             FROM claims cl JOIN sources s ON s.id = cl.source_id
            WHERE cl.company_id = ? ORDER BY cl.id""",
        (company_id,),
    ).fetchall()
    return [
        Claim(
            id=r["id"], person_id=r["person_id"], source_id=r["source_id"],
            claim_type=r["claim_type"], tier=r["tier"], source_type=r["source_type"],
            as_of_date=date.fromisoformat(r["as_of_date"]), as_of_basis=r["as_of_basis"],
            effective_date=date.fromisoformat(r["effective_date"]) if r["effective_date"] else None,
            raw_title=r["raw_title"], level=r["level"], department=r["department"],
            canonical_role=r["canonical_role"], departure_scope=r["departure_scope"],
        )
        for r in rows
    ]


def rebuild_roles(conn: sqlite3.Connection, company_id: int, today: date,
                  freshness_months: int = 12) -> int:
    """Recompute roles and employment status for one company from its claims.

    Idempotent: running it twice gives the same rows. Returns the role count.
    """
    result = resolve(load_claims(conn, company_id), today, freshness_months)
    iso = lambda d: d.isoformat() if d else None  # noqa: E731
    with conn:
        conn.execute("DELETE FROM roles WHERE company_id = ?", (company_id,))
        conn.executemany(
            """INSERT INTO roles (company_id, person_id, title, level, department,
                   canonical_role, status, status_reason, ended_on, ended_by_claim_id,
                   first_seen, last_seen, conflict, conflict_reason,
                   conflicting_claim_id, source_count, supporting_claim_id)
               VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?)""",
            [(company_id, r.person_id, r.title, r.level, r.department, r.canonical_role,
              r.status, r.status_reason, iso(r.ended_on), r.ended_by_claim_id,
              iso(r.first_seen), iso(r.last_seen), int(r.conflict), r.conflict_reason,
              r.conflicting_claim_id, r.source_count, r.supporting_claim_id)
             for r in result.roles],
        )
        conn.execute("UPDATE people SET employment_status = 'unknown' WHERE company_id = ?",
                     (company_id,))
        conn.executemany(
            "UPDATE people SET employment_status = ? WHERE id = ? AND company_id = ?",
            [(status, pid, company_id) for pid, status in result.employment.items()],
        )
    return len(result.roles)

"""Print every worked case of the role resolution rules as a table.

    uv run python tools/show_cases.py

For manual review against SPEC section 3.6: each row shows what the rules
actually return for one situation, and whether that matches the expectation
written in tests/worked_cases.py. X and Y are two people.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
sys.path[:0] = [str(ROOT), str(ROOT / "tests")]

from worked_cases import CASES, TODAY  # noqa: E402

from leadership.resolve import resolve  # noqa: E402

NAMES = {1: "X", 2: "Y"}


def main() -> int:
    wrong = 0
    for n, case in enumerate(CASES, 1):
        today = case.get("today", TODAY)
        result = resolve(case["claims"], today)
        got = {(r.person_id, r.key): r for r in result.roles}
        ok = ({k: (r.status, r.status_reason) for k, r in got.items()} == case["expect"]
              and result.employment == case["employment"])
        wrong += not ok
        print(f"\n{n:>2}. {case['name']}   [as of {today}]   {'OK' if ok else 'MISMATCH'}")
        for (pid, key), r in sorted(got.items()):
            extra = ""
            if r.ended_on:
                extra += f"  ends {r.ended_on}"
            if r.conflict:
                extra += f"  CONFLICT: {r.conflict_reason}"
            print(f"      {NAMES[pid]} as {key:<20} {r.status:<11} {r.status_reason}{extra}")
        print("      employment: " + ", ".join(
            f"{NAMES[p]}={s}" for p, s in sorted(result.employment.items())))
    print(f"\n{len(CASES) - wrong} of {len(CASES)} cases match their expected outcome")
    return 1 if wrong else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

import random
from datetime import date

import pytest
from worked_cases import (CASES, CEO, CFO, CTO, TODAY, X, Y, appointment, departure,
                          filing, live, news, release)

from leadership.resolve import CURRENT, UNVERIFIED, resolve, role_key


def _by_key(result):
    return {(r.person_id, r.key): r for r in result.roles}

\[REDACTED]("case", CASES, ids=[c["name"] for c in CASES])
def test_worked_case(case):
    result = resolve(case["claims"], case.get("today", TODAY))
    got = {k: (r.status, r.status_reason) for k, r in _by_key(result).items()}
    assert got == case["expect"]
    assert result.employment == case["employment"]


def test_every_role_names_the_rule_that_decided_it():
    for case in CASES:
        for r in resolve(case["claims"], case.get("today", TODAY)).roles:
            assert r.status_reason.startswith("rule")


def test_resolve_is_pure_and_order_independent():
    for case in CASES:
        claims = list(case["claims"])
        today = case.get("today", TODAY)
        first = resolve(claims, today)
        shuffled = claims[:]
        random.Random(7).shuffle(shuffled)
        assert resolve(shuffled, today) == first       # input order does not matter
        assert resolve(claims, today) == first         # same input, same output
        assert claims == list(case["claims"])          # input not modified


def test_news_only_departure_records_the_evidence_and_the_reason():
    with_page = [live(1, X, "CTO", **CTO),
                 departure(2, X, "role", tier=3, src="news", on=date(2026, 10, 1), title="CTO", **CTO)]
    r = _by_key(resolve(with_page, TODAY))[(X, "CTO")]
    assert r.conflict and r.conflicting_claim_id == 2
    assert "company page still lists the role" in r.conflict_reason

    without_page = [release(1, X, "CTO", date(2026, 3, 1), **CTO),
                    departure(2, X, "role", tier=3, src="news", on=date(2026, 9, 1), title="CTO", **CTO)]
    r = _by_key(resolve(without_page, TODAY))[(X, "CTO")]
    assert r.status == UNVERIFIED                      # never 'former' on news alone
    assert r.conflict and r.conflicting_claim_id == 2
    assert "no company source confirms" in r.conflict_reason


def test_lower_tier_source_raises_a_conflict_instead_of_overriding():
    roles = _by_key(resolve([live(1, X, "CTO", **CTO),
                             news(2, Y, "CTO", date(2026, 10, 10), **CTO)], TODAY))
    loser, winner = roles[(Y, "CTO")], roles[(X, "CTO")]
    assert winner.status == CURRENT and winner.conflict

2	
3	Claims are append-only observations. Roles and employment status are derived:
4	`rebuild_roles` deletes and recomputes them from claims with the pure function
5	`resolve.resolve`, so they can be regenerated at any time. See SPEC section 4.
6	"""

18	    id            INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,

21	    collected_at  TEXT
22	);

27	    started_at   TEXT NOT NULL,
28	    finished_at  TEXT,
29	    status       TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'running' CHECK (status IN
30	                 ('running','complete','budget_exhausted','insufficient_data',
31	                  'partial_failure','interrupted')),
32	    reasons      TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]',   -- JSON list: every condition that applied
33	    counters     TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'    -- JSON: usage against each limit
34	);
35	
36	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS sources (
37	    id            INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
38	    company_id    INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES companies(id),
39	    url           TEXT NOT NULL,
40	    source_type   TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (source_type IN
41	                  ('company_site','sec_filing','press_release','news','wikipedia','search_snippet')),
42	    tier          INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (tier BETWEEN 1 AND 4),
43	    title         TEXT,
44	    published_at  TEXT,                         -- NULL when unknown; never guessed
45	    retrieved_at  TEXT NOT NULL,
46	    content_hash  TEXT,
47	    stage         TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'fetched' CHECK (stage IN
48	                  ('fetched','extracted','failed','skipped')),
49	    attempts      INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
50	    last_error    TEXT,
51	    UNIQUE (company_id, url)
52	);
53	
54	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS people (
55	    id                 INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
56	    company_id         INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES companies(id),
57	    full_name          TEXT NOT NULL,
58	    normalized_name    TEXT NOT NULL,
59	    linkedin_url       TEXT,
60	    employment_status  TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'unknown' CHECK (employment_status IN
61	                       ('current','former','unknown'))      -- DERIVED
62	);
63	
64	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS claims (
65	    id                  INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
66	    company_id          INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES companies(id),
67	    person_id           INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES people(id),
68	    source_id           INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES sources(id),
69	    claim_type          TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (claim_type IN
70	                        ('role','appointment','departure','location','bio')),
71	    departure_scope     TEXT CHECK (departure_scope IN ('role','company')),
72	    raw_title           TEXT,
73	    level               TEXT CHECK (level IN ('c_level','vp','head','other')),
74	    department          TEXT,
75	    canonical_role      TEXT,
76	    value               TEXT,                   -- location / bio text
77	    evidence            TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(trim(evidence)) > 0),
78	    as_of_date          TEXT NOT NULL,          -- ISO date
79	    as_of_basis         TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (as_of_basis IN ('published','retrieved')),
80	    effective_date      TEXT,                   -- stated in the text, if any
81	    extraction_version  TEXT NOT NULL,
82	    CHECK (claim_type <> 'departure' OR departure_scope IS NOT NULL)
83	);
84	
85	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS roles (                -- DERIVED, rebuilt by rebuild_roles
86	    id                    INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
87	    company_id            INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES companies(id),
88	    person_id             INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES people(id),
89	    title                 TEXT NOT NULL,
90	    level                 TEXT,

97	    first_seen            TEXT,

108	CREATE VIEW IF NOT EXISTS leadership AS
109	SELECT
110	    c.domain               AS company_domain,
111	    c.name                 AS company,
112	    p.full_name            AS person,

114	    r.title, r.level, r.department, r.canonical_role,
115	    r.status, r.status_reason, r.ended_on,
116	    r.first_seen, r.last_seen, r.last_verified_at,
117	    r.conflict, r.conflict_reason, r.source_count,
118	    (SELECT l.value FROM claims l JOIN sources ls ON ls.id = l.source_id
119	      WHERE l.person_id = p.id AND l.claim_type = 'location'
120	      ORDER BY ls.tier, l.as_of_date DESC, l.id LIMIT 1)        AS location,
121	    (SELECT ls.url FROM claims l JOIN sources ls ON ls.id = l.source_id
122	      WHERE l.person_id = p.id AND l.claim_type = 'location'
123	      ORDER BY ls.tier, l.as_of_date DESC, l.id LIMIT 1)        AS location_source_url,
124	    (SELECT l.value FROM claims l JOIN sources ls ON ls.id = l.source_id
125	      WHERE l.person_id = p.id AND l.claim_type = 'bio'
126	      ORDER BY ls.tier, l.as_of_date DESC, l.id LIMIT 1)        AS bio,
127	    s.url                  AS source_url,
128	    s.source_type          AS source_type,
129	    sc.as_of_date          AS source_date,
130	    substr(sc.evidence, 1, 300) AS evidence,
131	    cs.url                 AS conflicting_source_url,
132	    substr(cc.evidence, 1, 300) AS conflicting_evidence
133	FROM roles r
134	JOIN people p     ON p.id = r.person_id
135	JOIN companies c  ON c.id = r.company_id
136	LEFT JOIN claims sc  ON sc.id = r.supporting_claim_id
137	LEFT JOIN sources s  ON s.id = sc.source_id
138	LEFT JOIN claims cc  ON cc.id = r.conflicting_claim_id
139	LEFT JOIN sources cs ON cs.id = cc.source_id;

141	CREATE VIEW IF NOT EXISTS current_leadership AS
142	SELECT * FROM leadership
143	WHERE status = 'current' AND level IN ('c_level', 'vp', 'head');

147	def connect(path: str | Path) -> sqlite3.Connection:
148	    """Open (and create if needed) the database with the schema applied."""
149	    conn = sqlite3.connect(str(path))
150	    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
151	    conn.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON")
152	    conn.executescript(SCHEMA)
153	    return conn
154	
155	
156	def load_claims(conn: sqlite3.Connection, company_id: int) -> list[Claim]:
157	    rows = conn.execute(
158	        """SELECT cl.*, s.tier, s.source_type
159	             FROM claims cl JOIN sources s ON s.id = cl.source_id
160	            WHERE cl.company_id = ? ORDER BY cl.id""",
161	        (company_id,),
162	    ).fetchall()
163	    return [
164	        Claim(
165	            id=r["id"], person_id=r["person_id"], source_id=r["source_id"],
166	            claim_type=r["claim_type"], tier=r["tier"], source_type=r["source_type"],
167	            as_of_date=date.fromisoformat(r["as_of_date"]), as_of_basis=r["as_of_basis"],
168	            effective_date=date.fromisoformat(r["effective_date"]) if r["effective_date"] else None,
169	            raw_title=r["raw_title"], level=r["level"], department=r["department"],
170	            canonical_role=r["canonical_role"], departure_scope=r["departure_scope"],
171	        )
172	        for r in rows
173	    ]
174	
175	
176	def rebuild_roles(conn: sqlite3.Connection, company_id: int, today: date,
177	                  freshness_months: int = 12) -> int:
178	    """Recompute roles and employment status for one company from its claims.
179	
180	    Idempotent: running it twice gives the same rows. Returns the role count.
181	    """
182	    result = resolve(load_claims(conn, company_id), today, freshness_months)
183	    iso = lambda d: d.isoformat() if d else None  # noqa: E731
184	    with conn:
185	        conn.execute("DELETE FROM roles WHERE company_id = ?", (company_id,))
186	        conn.executemany(
187	            """INSERT INTO roles (company_id, person_id, title, level, department,
188	                   canonical_role, status, status_reason, ended_on, ended_by_claim_id,
189	                   first_seen, last_seen, conflict, conflict_reason,
190	                   conflicting_claim_id, source_count, supporting_claim_id)
191	               VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?)""",
192	            [(company_id, r.person_id, r.title, r.level, r.department, r.canonical_role,
193	              r.status, r.status_reason, iso(r.ended_on), r.ended_by_claim_id,
194	              iso(r.first_seen), iso(r.last_seen), int(r.conflict), r.conflict_reason,
195	              r.conflicting_claim_id, r.source_count, r.supporting_claim_id)
196	             for r in result.roles],
197	        )
198	        conn.execute("UPDATE people SET employment_status = 'unknown' WHERE company_id = ?",
199	                     (company_id,))
200	        conn.executemany(
201	            "UPDATE people SET employment_status = ? WHERE id = ? AND company_id = ?",
202	            [(status, pid, company_id) for pid, status in result.employment.items()],
203	        )
204	    return len(result.roles)
