tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SearchPlugins
tools.description:
Search the user's claude.ai plugin catalog by keyword. Call this when a plugin (slash command, skill bundle, hook, or agent) from the user's org catalog might help complete the task. The user does not need to name a plugin: search when the task depends on their team's own process, systems or data and nothing you already have, the project's own scripts included, covers it.

Examples:
- "use the deploy plugin" → keywords ["deploy"]
- "is there something for linting?" → keywords ["lint", "format", "code quality"]
- "ship this to staging" → keywords ["deploy", "release", "staging"]
- "review this contract against our playbook" → keywords ["legal", "contract", "playbook"]
- "which deals close this week?" → keywords ["sales", "pipeline", "crm"]

Do not search unasked for one-off questions or tasks you can handle directly ("explain this regex", "fix this typo"), or after the user ignored a suggestion in this conversation.

Returns a ranked list with id, name, description, and whether the plugin is already enabled for this session (in a channel session, whether the channel has it). When results fit and SuggestPluginInstall is among your tools, call it to render the install card; otherwise relay the relevant results in text instead. If nothing relevant, proceed without mentioning that you searched.

tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.description:
Withdraw a proposal you made with start_session (initiation "own_initiative" or "offer") that the user has not started.

Call this when it went stale: the work was done here after all (by you or the user), it turned out unnecessary, or you proposed a better-scoped replacement (propose the new one first, then dismiss the old task_id). A card the user answered has already left, "Do it here" included, so it needs no call.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__hand_off_to_session
tools.description: Move the task you are in the middle of into its own session (a fork of this conversation plus your remaining plan) so you can answer the user now. Use it when a new user message about something else arrives mid-task — not for small corrections or when the user said to keep the work here. In a worktree the fork gets a fresh worktree, normally cut from your branch tip: commit first (uncommitted edits stay here). Bold title line and one sentence right before the call; after it, stop that task here and answer the new message — no recap.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

scope.description: Required with items: "first_task", "continuation" or "new_task" (see the tool description). Omit on advance / done / start updates.

session.description: When you delegated this step to a session you started: that session's short name (from start_session's result). The app shows its live state on the step.

items.description: The whole plan, in order (1–12 steps); replaces the previous list.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields (write recap last) — ask and recap are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Like the recap, never point at anything else in the conversation. Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available, or one your own work this turn made available; others are refused, and one that later stops being available is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and other answers), so do not guess. Offer commit, create_pr or verify only once the work the user asked for is done, not every turn. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Not now": a button, not a sentence. A click sends it to you as the user's answer. Never a go-ahead to commit: that is the commit app action. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action.

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments. Never repeat an offer the user passed over, as an app action, a reply or a question in your closing message, unless what it acts on has changed since or they bring it up.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

"""Probe: which stored third-party pages name the company's own domain? Reads the cache only."""
import json
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

root = Path(sys.argv[1])
sys.path.insert(0, str(root))
from leadership.db import connect  # noqa: E402
from leadership.sources.web import clean_text, find_title  # noqa: E402

pages = {}
for f in (root / "cache" / "pages").glob("*"):
    try:
        e = json.loads(f.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    except Exception:
        continue
    v = e.get("value") or {}
    pages[e.get("key")] = v

conn = connect(root / "data" / "leadership.db")
for dom, own in (("meetcampfire.com", ["meetcampfire.com", "campfire.ai"]),
                 ("robinhood.com", ["robinhood.com"])):
    pat = re.compile(r"(?<![a-z0-9-])(?:" + "|".join(map(re.escape, own)) + r")(?![a-z0-9-])")
    cid = conn.execute("SELECT id FROM companies WHERE domain=?", (dom,)).fetchone()["id"]
    for s in conn.execute("SELECT url FROM sources WHERE company_id=? AND tier=3", (cid,)):
        v = next((v for k, v in pages.items() if k and s["url"] in k), None)
        if v is None:
            print("NO CACHE", s["url"])
            continue
        body = v.get("body") or ""
        raw = len(pat.findall(body.lower()))
        text = clean_text(body)
        print(f"raw={raw:<3} text={len(pat.findall(text.lower())):<3} len={len(text):<6} {s['url'][:70]}")
        print("     title:", (find_title(body) or "")[:90].encode("ascii", "replace").decode())
        if "thecampfire" in s["url"] or "tavily.com" in s["url"]:
            print("     text:", text[:500].encode("ascii", "replace").decode())

plan += [Planned(f.url, "sec_filing", 1, f.filed, sec_headers) for f in filings]

        wiki_url, wiki_headers, note = wikipedia.find_article(fetcher, site.name, site.domains)
        notes.append("Wikipedia: " + note)
        log.event("discover", source="wikipedia", note=note)
        if wiki_url:
            plan.append(Planned(wiki_url, "wikipedia", 3, headers=wiki_headers))

        if not search.available:
            notes.append("web search: skipped, TAVILY_API_KEY is not set")
        elif cfg.limits.max_search_rounds < 1:
            notes.append("web search: skipped, max_search_rounds is 0")
        else:
            results = []
            for q in round_one_queries(site.name, registrable(urlsplit(site.home_url).netloc)):
                cached = search.cache.get(f"tavily|{search.max_results}|{q}") and not refresh
                if not cached and not budget.take("search_queries", "discover"):
                    break
                try:
                    found, _ = search.query(q)
                except SearchError as e:
                    add_reason(reasons, "partial_failure", "discover", f"web search failed: {e}", query=q)
                    break
                results += found
            planned_urls = {p.url for p in plan}
            usable = [r for r in results if r["url"] not in planned_urls
                      and registrable(urlsplit(r["url"]).netloc) not in _NO_FETCH]
            # Namesakes are common ("Campfire"): keep only results about this company.
            if llm is None or budget.take("llm_calls", "discover"):
                relevant, calls = pick_results(llm, site, usable, cfg.discovery.news_pages,
                                               FileCache(root / "cache" / "llm"), log, problems)
                if llm is not None:
                    counters["llm_calls"] += calls - 1
            else:
                relevant = []
            dates = {r["url"]: result_date(r.get("published_date")) for r in usable}
            for u in relevant:
                plan.append(Planned(u, *classify(u, site.domains), dates.get(u)))
            notes.append(f"web search: {len(results)} results, {len(usable)} usable, "
                         f"{len(relevant)} about this company and added")
        for problem in problems:
            add_reason(reasons, "partial_failure", "discover", problem)
            notes.append("degraded: " + problem)
        counters["sources_found"] = len(plan)
        save_run()

        # --------------------------------------------------------------- fetch
        for p in plan:
            row = conn.execute("SELECT * FROM sources WHERE company_id = ? AND url = ?",
                               (company_id, p.url)).fetchone()
            if row and not refresh and row["stage"] in ("fetched", "extracted", "skipped"):
                continue                            # done in an earlier run or before a resume
            if row and row["stage"] == "failed" and row["attempts"] >= cfg.limits.max_source_attempts:
                add_reason(reasons, "partial_failure", "fetch",
                           f"gave up after {row['attempts']} attempts: {row['last_error']}", url=p.url)
                continue
            if not budget.take("pages", "fetch"):
                break
            page = fetcher.get(p.url, headers=p.headers)
            if page.ok:
                stage, error = "fetched", None
                published = p.published_at
                if not published and p.source_type in ("press_release", "news"):
                    published = find_published(page.body)   # a page's own stated date only
                digest, title = content_hash(page.body), find_title(page.body)
            else:
                published, digest, title = p.published_at, None, None
                error = page.error
                if error and "robots" in error:
                    stage = "skipped"
                    counters["pages_skipped"] += 1
                else:
                    stage = "failed"
                    counters["pages_failed"] += 1
                    add_reason(reasons, "partial_failure", "fetch", error, url=p.url)
            # Saved immediately, one transaction per source, so a crash loses nothing.
            conn.execute(
                """INSERT INTO sources (company_id, url, source_type, tier, title, published_at,
                       retrieved_at, content_hash, stage, attempts, last_error)
                   VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,1,?)
                   ON CONFLICT(company_id, url) DO UPDATE SET
                       title = excluded.title, published_at = excluded.published_at,
                       retrieved_at = excluded.retrieved_at, content_hash = excluded.content_hash,
                       stage = excluded.stage, attempts = sources.attempts + 1,
                       last_error = excluded.last_error""",
                (company_id, p.url, p.source_type, p.tier, title, published,
                 page.retrieved_at or _now(), digest, stage, error))
            save_run()

        # ----------------------------------------------------------------- end
        have = conn.execute(
            "SELECT count(*) FROM sources WHERE company_id = ? AND stage IN ('fetched','extracted') "
            "AND source_type IN ('company_site','press_release')", (company_id,)).fetchone()[0]
        if have <= 1:       # the homepage alone says little about leadership
            add_reason(reasons, "insufficient_data", "discover",
                       "no company page other than the homepage could be read")
        counters["network_calls_this_process"] = fetcher.network_calls + search.network_calls
        status = headline(reasons)
        save_run(status)
        conn.execute("UPDATE companies SET collected_at = ? WHERE id = ?", (_now(), company_id))
        conn.commit()
        log.event("run_end", run_id=run_id, status=status, reasons=reasons, counters=counters,
                  limits={k: getattr(cfg.limits, v) for k, v in Budget.LIMITS.items()})
        return RunResult(run_id, site.name, status, reasons, counters,
                         fetcher.network_calls + search.network_calls, log.path, notes)
    finally:
        fetcher.close()
        search.close()
        conn.close()


def _db_path(root: Path) -> Path:
    path = root / "data" / "leadership.db"
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    return path


def print_report(result: RunResult, cfg: Config, conn_path: Path) -> None:
    """Usage against each limit, every reason, and what was stored."""
    c = result.counters
    print(f"\nCompany:  {result.company}")
    print(f"Run:      {result.run_id}    Status: {result.status}")
    for note in result.notes:
        print(f"  - {note}")
    print("\nUsage against limits")
    for name, limit in Budget.LIMITS.items():
        print(f"  {name:<16}{c.get(name, 0):>4} of {getattr(cfg.limits, limit)}")
    print(f"  {'pages failed':<16}{c.get('pages_failed', 0):>4}")
    print(f"  {'pages skipped':<16}{c.get('pages_skipped', 0):>4}   (robots.txt)")
    print(f"  {'network calls':<16}{result.network_calls:>4}   (this process; 0 means all from cache)")
    if result.reasons:
        print("\nReasons recorded")
        for r in result.reasons:
            where = f"  [{r['url']}]" if r.get("url") else ""
            print(f"  {r['code']:<18}{r['stage']:<9}{r['detail']}{where}")

class FakeWeb:
    """Serves the fake site and counts every request that reaches the network layer."""

    def __init__(self, broken=("/about/team-archive",)):
        self.requests, self.broken = [], set(broken)
        self.transport = httpx.MockTransport(self.handle)

    def handle(self, request: httpx.Request) -> httpx.Response:
        self.requests.append(str(request.url))
        host, path = request.url.host, request.url.path
        if host == "old-acme.com":
            return httpx.Response(301, headers={"location": f"https://acme-robotics.com{path}"})
        if host == "en.wikipedia.org":
            return httpx.Response(200, json={"query": {"search": []}})
        if host == "api.tavily.com":
            return httpx.Response(200, json={"results": [
                {"title": "Acme hires CTO", "url": "https://technews.example/acme-cto",
                 "content": "Acme Robotics (acme-robotics.com) hired a CTO.",
                 "published_date": "Fri, 02 Oct 2026 09:30:00 GMT"},
                {"title": "Acme Robotics Club elects president", "url": "https://school.example/club",
                 "content": "The student robotics club named a new president."},
                {"title": "Profile", "url": "https://www.linkedin.com/in/someone", "content": "x"}]})
        if host == "technews.example":
            return httpx.Response(200, text="<html><title>Acme hires CTO</title><body>Story</body></html>")
        if host != "acme-robotics.com":
            return httpx.Response(500)
        if path in self.broken:
            return httpx.Response(500)
        if path in PAGES:
            return httpx.Response(200, text=PAGES[path])
        return httpx.Response(404)

    assert (news["source_type"], news["tier"], news["published_at"]) == ("news", 3, "2026-10-02")
    assert conn.execute("SELECT count(*) FROM sources WHERE url LIKE '%linkedin%'").fetchone()[0] == 0
    # A namesake that never mentions the company's domain is not stored as a source.
    assert conn.execute("SELECT count(*) FROM sources WHERE url LIKE '%school.example%'").fetchone()[0] == 0
    conn.close()
    log = result.log_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    events = [json.loads(line) for line in log.splitlines()]
    kinds = {e["event"] for e in events}

class FakeWeb:
    """Serves the fake site and counts every request that reaches the network layer."""

    def __init__(self, broken=("/about/team-archive",)):
        self.requests, self.broken = [], set(broken)
        self.transport = httpx.MockTransport(self.handle)

    def handle(self, request: httpx.Request) -> httpx.Response:
        self.requests.append(str(request.url))
        host, path = request.url.host, request.url.path
        if host == "old-acme.com":
            return httpx.Response(301, headers={"location": f"https://acme-robotics.com{path}"})
        if host == "en.wikipedia.org":
            return httpx.Response(200, json={"query": {"search": []}})
        if host == "api.tavily.com":
            return httpx.Response(200, json={"results": [
                {"title": "Acme hires CTO", "url": "https://technews.example/acme-cto",
                 "content": "Acme Robotics (acme-robotics.com) hired a CTO.",
                 "published_date": "Fri, 02 Oct 2026 09:30:00 GMT"},
                {"title": "Acme Robotics Club elects president", "url": "https://school.example/club",
                 "content": "The student robotics club named a new president."},
                {"title": "Profile", "url": "https://www.linkedin.com/in/someone", "content": "x"}]})
        if host == "technews.example":
            return httpx.Response(200, text="<html><title>Acme hires CTO</title><body>Story</body></html>")
        if host != "acme-robotics.com":
            return httpx.Response(500)
        if path in self.broken:
            return httpx.Response(500)
        if path in PAGES:
            return httpx.Response(200, text=PAGES[path])
        return httpx.Response(404)

def test_search_results_are_fetched_cached_and_the_key_stays_out_of_the_log(tmp_path, no_keys, monkeypatch):
    secret = "tvly-TESTSECRETVALUE0123456789"
    monkeypatch.setenv("TAVILY_API_KEY", secret)
    web = FakeWeb(broken=())
    result = _run(tmp_path, web)
    assert result.counters["search_queries"] == 4
    conn = connect(tmp_path / "data" / "leadership.db")
    news = conn.execute("SELECT * FROM sources WHERE url = 'https://technews.example/acme-cto'").fetchone()
    assert (news["source_type"], news["tier"], news["published_at"]) == ("news", 3, "2026-10-02")
    assert conn.execute("SELECT count(*) FROM sources WHERE url LIKE '%linkedin%'").fetchone()[0] == 0
    # A namesake that never mentions the company's domain is not stored as a source.
    assert conn.execute("SELECT count(*) FROM sources WHERE url LIKE '%school.example%'").fetchone()[0] == 0
    conn.close()
    log = result.log_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    events = [json.loads(line) for line in log.splitlines()]
    kinds = {e["event"] for e in events}
    assert {"run_start", "fetch", "search", "run_end"} <= kinds
    assert secret not in log and "Authorization" not in log
    end = events[-1]
    assert end["event"] == "run_end" and end["status"] == "complete"
    assert end["counters"]["search_queries"] == 4 and end["limits"]["search_queries"] == 25
    before = len(web.requests)
    second = _run(tmp_path, web)
    assert len(web.requests) == before and second.counters["search_queries"] == 0

1	# M2 acceptance report: discovery, fetch, cache, limits, logging
2	
3	- **Run date:** 2026-11-12
4	- **Branch:** `m2-collect` (log captured before the M2 commit, on top of `0db4a23`)
5	- **Raw evidence:** [M2_results.log](M2_results.log) — full, unedited command output
6	- **Reproduce:** `uv run python tools/acceptance.py M2`
7	- **Needs:** network, and the keys in `.env`. It makes real requests to the two
8	  company sites, the SEC, the search provider (8 queries) and the LLM provider.
9	
10	## 1. Automated results
11	
12	All numbers below are copied from `M2_results.log`.
13	
14	| # | Step | Expected | Actual | Result |
15	|---|---|---|---|---|
16	| 1 | M2 tests | all pass | 45 passed | PASS |
17	| 2 | Whole fast suite | all pass | 162 passed, 6 deselected (the 6 need keys) | PASS |
18	| 3 | Real-model tests | all pass | 2 passed | PASS |
19	| 4 | Campfire, caches ignored | status `complete` | `complete`; 17 pages, 4 search queries, 33 network calls | PASS |
20	| 5 | Campfire, second run | 0 network calls | `complete`; 0 pages, 0 queries, 0 network calls | PASS |
21	| 6 | Robinhood, caches ignored | status `complete` | `complete`; 27 pages (20 fetched, 7 skipped), 38 network calls | PASS |
22	| 7 | Robinhood, second run | 0 network calls | `complete`; 0 network calls | PASS |
23	| 8 | Campfire stored data | listing | 17 sources, all fetched; 2 articles without a date | PASS |
24	| 9 | Robinhood stored data | listing | 27 sources: 5 SEC filings, 13 company newsroom articles | PASS |
25	| 10 | Unreachable homepage | exit code 1, nothing stored | "Stopped: Could not read the homepage ... Nothing was stored." | PASS |
26	| 11 | Secret scan | 0 problems | 58 files scanned (16 of them run logs), 0 problems | PASS |
27	
28	11 of 11 steps as expected.
29	
30	The fast tests use a small website served in memory. The real fetcher, cache,
31	robots handling, budgets, database and run log run unchanged; only the
32	network is replaced. No model is faked: without a key the pipeline's own
33	keyword ranking is used, and the two real-model tests call the real provider.
34	
35	## 2. M2 acceptance criteria (SPEC section 8)
36	
37	| Criterion | Status | Evidence |
38	|---|---|---|
39	| Both companies: at least one company-site team page found | **Not met as written** | See below |
40	| Robinhood includes at least one SEC filing | Met | 5 filings fetched (step 9) |
41	| A second run makes zero network calls | Met | Steps 5 and 7; `test_second_run_makes_no_network_calls` |
42	| Limits enforced from `config.toml` | Met | `test_page_budget_stops_the_run_and_names_the_limit`, `test_search_query_budget_is_enforced`, `test_resume_cannot_bypass_the_budget` |
43	| Run status and run log written | Met | Steps 8 and 9; `test_search_results_are_fetched_cached_and_the_key_stays_out_of_the_log` |
44	
45	**The team-page criterion.** Neither company gave a readable team page, for
46	different reasons:
47	
48	- **Campfire has no team or about page.** Its sitemap lists 262 pages and
49	  none is one; `/about` returns 404. What was collected instead: 9 posts from
50	  its own blog, including the stealth-launch, Series A and Series B
51	  announcements, and 7 third-party articles (for example CFO Dive and an
52	  interview with its CEO).
53	- **Robinhood's leadership page was found but could not be read.** Search
54	  returned `investors.robinhood.com/governance/leadership`, but that site
55	  refuses automated clients (it answers 403, including for `robots.txt`).
56	  The page is stored as `skipped`. What was collected instead: 5 SEC filings
57	  and 13 newsroom articles about executive appointments.
58	
59	So for Robinhood, current roles will rest on SEC filings (tier 1) and company
60	press releases (tier 2). For Campfire they will rest on company blog posts
61	(tier 2) and news (tier 3). Neither will have a "live page listing" (rule 4).
62	This is a property of the two sites, not something more code can fix without
63	pretending to be a browser, which I did not do.
64	
65	## 3. Checklist rows covered
66	
67	| Row | Requirement (short) | Evidence |
68	|---|---|---|
69	| R16 | Domain or URL accepted; company name derived | Steps 4, 6; `test_company_name_from_site_metadata` |

  company sites, the SEC, the search provider (8 queries) and the LLM provider.

## 1. Automated results

All numbers below are copied from `M2_results.log`.

11 of 11 steps as expected.

The fast tests use a small website served in memory. The real fetcher, cache,
robots handling, budgets, database and run log run unchanged; only the
network is replaced. No model is faked: without a key the pipeline's own
keyword ranking is used, and the two real-model tests call the real provider.

## 2. M2 acceptance criteria (SPEC section 8)

**The team-page criterion.** Neither company gave a readable team page, for
different reasons:

- **Campfire has no team or about page.** Its sitemap lists 262 pages and
  none is one; `/about` returns 404. What was collected instead: 9 posts from
  its own blog, including the stealth-launch, Series A and Series B
  announcements, and 7 third-party articles (for example CFO Dive and an

  refuses automated clients (it answers 403, including for `robots.txt`).
  The page is stored as `skipped`. What was collected instead: 5 SEC filings
  and 13 newsroom articles about executive appointments.

press releases (tier 2). For Campfire they will rest on company blog posts
(tier 2) and news (tier 3). Neither will have a "live page listing" (rule 4).

pretending to be a browser, which I did not do.

appeared in the input, so it cannot invent addresses.
- **Search round 1** (if a key is configured): a fixed set of four queries,
  each anchored with the company's domain, such as
  `"<company>" <domain> leadership team` and `"<company>" <domain> "head of"`.
- **Namesake filter.** Other organisations often share a company's name. One
  LLM call keeps only the results that are about this company, given its
  website and the homepage's own description; its answer is filtered to URLs
  that were offered. Without a model, or if its answer is unusable, only
  results that name the company's domain are kept. LinkedIn and other social
  sites are never fetched.
- **Search round 2** runs only when triggered (section 3.10).
- **EDGAR** (if the company matches a public registrant): latest 10-K, latest
  proxy statement, and recent 8-K filings reporting officer changes (item
  5.02). Matching is strict: the registrant's name must equal the company's
  name once corporate words are removed, and its listed website, if any, must
  be the same domain. Needs `SEC_USER_AGENT`.
- **Wikipedia**: the company page, accepted only if it mentions the company's
  domain. Wikimedia refuses clients without contact details, so this runs
  only when `WIKIPEDIA_USER_AGENT` is set; otherwise it is skipped.
- **If a model call fails** during discovery (for example invalid JSON): one
  retry, then the keyword ranking is used and a `partial_failure` reason is
One bad page never stops a run.

### Known limits (to be stated in the README)

- A departure nobody announced publicly cannot be detected.
- VP and Head coverage for large companies is partial by nature.
- Personal location is often not public.
- A company's own page can state something false; it would still be stored as
  a tier-1 claim.

---

---

## 9. Open decisions

Decided:

- **Search API**: Tavily free tier, optional at run time.
- **Freshness window**: 12 months, applied only by rule 5 in section 3.6.
- **News-only departures**: always `unverified`, with the evidence and the
  conflict reason recorded (rule 2 in section 3.6).
- **Default limits** in section 3.10: agreed as starting values; M0 checks
  them against the free-tier quotas.
- **Run status precedence**: agreed, with every applicable reason recorded
  independently.
- **Thresholds**: precision ≥ 90%, gold C-level recall = 100%.

"""One-off patch: reworded team-page criterion, Wikipedia decision, lookalike exclusion (docs + checklist)."""
import copy
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from openpyxl import load_workbook
from openpyxl.formatting.formatting import ConditionalFormattingList

root = Path(sys.argv[1])


def patch(path, pairs):
    p = root / path
    s = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    for old, new in pairs:
        assert s.count(old) == 1, (path, old[:50], s.count(old))
        s = s.replace(old, new)
    p.write_text(s, encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")


patch("SPEC.md", [
 ("Status: **revision 6, 2026-11-12**", "Status: **revision 7, 2026-11-12**"),
 ('''results that name the company's domain are kept. LinkedIn and other social
  sites are never fetched.''', '''results that name the company's domain are kept. LinkedIn and other social
  sites are never fetched, and neither are the search provider's own
  generated summary pages.
- **Lookalike check.** A page found by search on a site whose name contains
  the company's name but is not the company's (thecampfire.ai for
  campfire.ai) is used only if the page itself names one of the company's
  domains. Otherwise it is stored with stage `skipped` and the reason, and
  its text is never extracted. This check is code, not a model decision.'''),
 ('''only when `WIKIPEDIA_USER_AGENT` is set; otherwise it is skipped.''',
  '''only when `WIKIPEDIA_USER_AGENT` is set; otherwise it is skipped.
  Decided 2026-11-12: it is not set for this project, so Wikipedia is not a

"""One-off patch: report, spec, README and checklist for the generated-summary exclusion."""
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from openpyxl import load_workbook

root = Path(sys.argv[1])


def patch(path, pairs):
    p = root / path
    s = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    for old, new in pairs:
        assert s.count(old) == 1, (path, old[:50], s.count(old))
        s = s.replace(old, new)
    p.write_text(s, encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")


patch("SPEC.md", [
 ('''sites are never fetched, and neither are the search provider's own
  generated summary pages.''', '''sites are never fetched.
- **Original sources only.** Machine-generated summary pages published by
  search companies (`tavily.com`, `exa.ai`) are never fetched or stored, so
  they can never be evidence for a claim. They may appear among search
  results, which is how other sources are found.'''),
 ('''- **Thresholds**: precision ≥ 90%, gold C-level recall = 100%.''',
  '''- **Generated summaries** (2026-11-12): pages generated by search companies
  are not evidence; only original sources are (section 3.1).
- **Thresholds**: precision ≥ 90%, gold C-level recall = 100%.'''),
])
patch("README.md", [
 ('''  otherwise it is recorded as `skipped` and never read for people.
''', '''  otherwise it is recorded as `skipped` and never read for people.
- **Original sources only.** Machine-generated summary pages from search
  companies (`tavily.com`, `exa.ai`) are never used as evidence.
'''),
])

 ("64 files scanned (21 of them run logs), 0 problems", "69 files scanned (26 of them run logs), 0 problems"),
 ("11 of 11 steps as expected.\n", '''11 of 11 steps as expected.

Source counts move by one or two between runs with `--refresh`, because the
search provider does not return exactly the same results each time. Between
the last two runs Campfire lost a CFO Dive article and Robinhood gained a

'''),

It is about the right company, but it is a summary, not an original source | Excluded, at your request: such pages (`tavily.com`, `exa.ai`) are never fetched or stored, so they cannot be evidence for a claim |

the company's. The three remaining Campfire news pages all name
`campfire.ai`. But one of the company's own blog posts'''),

        done += 1
assert done == 1
wb.properties.lastModifiedBy = ""
wb.properties.creator = ""
wb.save(path)
print("patched")

content.text:
Your Microsoft run behaved as built, and it exposed one inconsistency I'd like your decision on. I changed nothing.

## What the run shows

- **SEC matching worked on a third company:** it matched `MICROSOFT CORP` and fetched 5 filings.
- **12 sources were fetched**, including two leadership pages on `www.microsoft.com`.
- **4 pages answered HTTP 403**, which made the status `partial_failure`. Three are Microsoft's own (`news.microsoft.com/source/leadership`, the Satya Nadella profile, a blog author page) and one is `comparably.com`. Microsoft's main leadership page is among them, so it has the same limitation as Robinhood.

## The inconsistency

Microsoft and Robinhood both refuse automated clients, but the runs end differently:

| Site | How it refuses | Stored as | Run status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `investors.robinhood.com` | 403 on `robots.txt` | `skipped` | `complete` |
| `news.microsoft.com` | 403 on the page itself | `failed` | `partial_failure` |

I recommend recording a page-level 403 as `skipped` with the reason "the site refused automated access", the same as Robinhood. Retrying will not help, and it is not an error on our side. The catch is that the Microsoft run would then read `complete` even though its main leadership page was not read; the refused pages would still be listed in the report with the reason.

## Three other things I noticed

- **`vectorshift.ai/research/companies/microsoft/people` looks like another generated company profile**, the same kind as the Exa page. I have not read it to confirm. This is the limit I mentioned: the exclusion list is two named sites.
- **Some dates are doubtful.** The search provider gave 2014-02-04 for the Business Roundtable member page. That is the day Nadella became CEO, so it is not a publication date. M3 should not treat a search-provider date on a profile page as a publication date.
- **Only 1 of 20 shortlisted site links was chosen by the model.** The leadership pages came from search instead, so nothing was lost here, but it is thinner than for the other two companies.

If this was meant as MT-2.5, that test also needs the `max_pages = 5` steps to check the budget stop and resume.

class Budget:
    """Usage counters checked against config limits. Cumulative across resumes."""

    LIMITS = {"pages": "max_pages", "search_queries": "max_search_queries",
              "llm_calls": "max_llm_calls"}

    def __init__(self, limits, counters: dict, reasons: list[dict]):
        self.limits, self.c, self.reasons = limits, counters, reasons
        for name in ("pages", "pages_failed", "pages_skipped", "search_queries", "llm_calls",
                     "sources_found"):
            self.c.setdefault(name, 0)

    def take(self, name: str, stage: str) -> bool:
        limit = getattr(self.limits, self.LIMITS[name])
        if self.c[name] >= limit:
            add_reason(self.reasons, "budget_exhausted", stage,
                       f"{self.LIMITS[name]}={limit} reached", limit=self.LIMITS[name])
            return False
        self.c[name] += 1
        return True


def add_reason(reasons: list[dict], code: str, stage: str, detail: str, **extra) -> None:
    """Record a condition once per (code, stage, detail). Every condition is kept."""
    entry = {"code": code, "stage": stage, "detail": detail, **extra}
    if entry not in reasons:
        reasons.append(entry)

    codes = {r["code"] for r in reasons}
    return next((s for s in PRECEDENCE if s in codes), "complete")

"""One-off patch: refused pages are skipped and reported; only page-stated dates; vectorshift excluded."""
import sys
from pathlib import Path

root = Path(sys.argv[1])


def patch(path, pairs):
    p = root / path
    s = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    for old, new in pairs:
        assert s.count(old) == 1, (path, old[:50], s.count(old))
        s = s.replace(old, new)
    p.write_text(s, encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")

"""One-off patch: docs + checklist for refused pages, page-stated dates, vectorshift."""
import copy
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from openpyxl import load_workbook
from openpyxl.formatting.formatting import ConditionalFormattingList

root = Path(sys.argv[1])


def patch(path, pairs):
    p = root / path

        ws.cell(row=r, column=9).value = "Built 2026-11-12. Evidence: acceptance/M2.md section 4, issues 9, 10 and 13"
        seen.add(rid)

def bump(ref):
    return re.sub(rf"(\$?[A-I]\$?){old_last}\b", rf"\g<1>{new_last}", ref)


ws.auto_filter.ref = bump(ws.auto_filter.ref)

for cf in ws.conditional_formatting:

        new_cf.add(bump(str(cf.sqref)), rule)

for sheet in wb.worksheets:

wb.properties.lastModifiedBy = ""
wb.properties.creator = ""
wb.save(path)
print("rows", old_last, "->", new_last, "| new id", vals[0])

"""One-off patch: record the review of the 12 decisions and the two caveats; add the M3 follow-up row."""
import copy
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from openpyxl import load_workbook
from openpyxl.formatting.formatting import ConditionalFormattingList

root = Path(sys.argv[1])
p = root / "acceptance" / "M2.md"
s = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
pairs = [
 ("Please confirm or change these in manual test MT-2.9.\n",
  '''**Reviewed by you on 2026-11-12: all twelve accepted, with two caveats that
M3 must address.**

- **On decision 9:** a page naming the company's domain does not prove it
  belongs to the same company. The lookalike check is only a first filter.
  The real check is per person, in extraction (checklist R150).
- **On decision 10:** a list of excluded sites cannot be maintained
  indefinitely. M3 needs a rule that does not depend on site names
  (checklist R153): a claim supported only by third-party profile, directory
  or summary pages cannot make a role `current`.
'''),
 ("| Decisions you want changed (MT-2.9) | |",
  "| Decisions you want changed (MT-2.9) | None. All 12 accepted on 2026-11-12, with the two caveats in section 5 carried to M3 (R150, R153) |"),
]
for old, new in pairs:
    assert s.count(old) == 1, old[:40]
    s = s.replace(old, new)
p.write_text(s, encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")

path = root / "SPEC_checklist.xlsx"
wb = load_workbook(path)
ws = wb["Requirements"]
old_last = ws.max_row
while ws.cell(row=old_last, column=1).value is None:
    old_last -= 1
n = 0
for r in range(2, old_last + 1):
    if ws.cell(row=r, column=1).value == "R150":
        ws.cell(row=r, column=9).value = ("Also the real answer to the M2 lookalike caveat (2026-11-12): a page naming "
                                          "the company's domain does not prove the person is this company's")
        n += 1
assert n == 1
vals = [f"R{old_last:02d}", "Verification",
        "A claim supported only by third-party profile, directory or generated summary pages cannot make a role "
        "current. The rule does not depend on a list of site names",
        "P0", "M3", "A labelled directory page from a site not on the M2 exclusion list yields no current role by itself",
        "3.1, 3.6", "Not started",
        "From the M2 review, 2026-11-12: the exclusion list of four sites cannot be maintained indefinitely"]
new_last = old_last + 1
for c, v in enumerate(vals, 1):
    src = ws.cell(row=old_last, column=c)
    cell = ws.cell(row=new_last, column=c, value=v)
    cell.font, cell.border = copy.copy(src.font), copy.copy(src.border)
    cell.fill, cell.alignment = copy.copy(src.fill), copy.copy(src.alignment)


def bump(ref):
    return re.sub(rf"(\$?[A-I]\$?){old_last}\b", rf"\g<1>{new_last}", ref)


ws.auto_filter.ref = bump(ws.auto_filter.ref)
for dv in ws.data_validations.dataValidation:
    dv.sqref = type(dv.sqref)(bump(str(dv.sqref)))
new_cf = ConditionalFormattingList()
for cf in ws.conditional_formatting:
    for rule in cf.rules:
        new_cf.add(bump(str(cf.sqref)), rule)
ws.conditional_formatting = new_cf
for sheet in wb.worksheets:
    if sheet.title == "Requirements":
        continue
    for row in sheet.iter_rows():
        for cell in row:
            if isinstance(cell.value, str) and cell.value.startswith("="):
                cell.value = cell.value.replace(f"${old_last},", f"${new_last},").replace(f"${old_last})", f"${new_last})")
wb.properties.lastModifiedBy = ""
wb.properties.creator = ""
wb.save(path)
print("rows", old_last, "->", new_last, "| new id", vals[0])

        add_reason(reasons, "interrupted", "run", "the previous process stopped before finishing")
        conn.execute("UPDATE runs SET status = 'interrupted', reasons = ? WHERE id = ?",
                     (json.dumps(reasons), last["id"]))
        conn.commit()
        last = conn.execute("SELECT * FROM runs WHERE id = ?", (last["id"],)).fetchone()
    if last and last["status"] in RESUMABLE:
        # Counters carry over, so a restart cannot bypass a budget. Old reasons
        # are kept in the log; the list is rebuilt from what is true this time.
        conn.execute("UPDATE runs SET status = 'running', finished_at = NULL WHERE id = ?",
                     (last["id"],))
        conn.commit()
        return last["id"], json.loads(last["counters"]), [], f"resumed ({last['status']})"
    cur = conn.execute("INSERT INTO runs (company_id, started_at) VALUES (?, ?)",

                    max_results=cfg.discovery.search_results_per_query, **kw)

        except HomepageError as e:

        company_id = conn.execute("SELECT id FROM companies WHERE domain = ?", (domain,)).fetchone()[0]
        run_id, counters, reasons, mode = _open_run(conn, company_id)

                                          None if status == "running" else _now(), run_id))

        problems: list[str] = []            # model failures that forced a fallback

        llm = LLM(cfg, "extract") if configured_providers() else None
        if llm is None:
            notes.append("no LLM key: site pages chosen by keyword ranking")

                                       FileCache(root / "cache" / "llm"), log, problems)
            if llm is not None:
                counters["llm_calls"] += calls - 1  # cache hits do not count; a retry does
        else:
            picked = offered[:cfg.discovery.site_pages]
        plan += [Planned(u, *classify(u, site.domains)) for u in picked]
        notes.append(f"company site: {len(site.candidates)} links found, {len(offered)} shortlisted, "
                     f"{len(picked)} chosen")

        notes.append("SEC EDGAR: " + note)
        log.event("discover", source="edgar", note=note)
        if note.startswith("failed"):
            add_reason(reasons, "partial_failure", "discover", "SEC EDGAR: " + note)
        sec_headers = {"User-Agent": edgar.user_agent()}

"""Run the M2 manual tests that can be scripted, and save the full output.

    uv run python tools/manual_checks_m2.py

Writes acceptance/M2_manual_results.log. Uses as few outside calls as it can:

- MT-2.1 to MT-2.4b, 2.7 and 2.8 run the real commands on the working data,
  which is answered from the cache.
- MT-2.5 (limits and resume) runs Microsoft in a separate folder that holds a
  copy of the cache, with only `max_pages` changed. No search or model call.
- MT-2.6 (interrupt and resume) runs Campfire in a separate folder that holds
  the search and model caches but no pages, so the pages are really fetched
  and the process can be stopped in the middle. The process is killed
  outright, which is harsher than Ctrl+C: nothing gets a chance to clean up.

The separate folders are under data/manual_m2/ (not committed) and are
rebuilt on every run. config.toml and the working database are not changed
by MT-2.5 and MT-2.6.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import re
import shutil
import sqlite3
import subprocess
import sys
import time
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))
WORK = ROOT / "data" / "manual_m2"
PY = [sys.executable, str(Path(__file__).resolve()), "--drive"]
CLI = ["uv", "run", "leadership", "collect"]
SHOW = ["uv", "run", "python", "tools/show_run.py"]


def drive(root: str, url: str, max_pages: str) -> int:
    """One collection run in another folder, with only max_pages overridden."""
    from leadership.collect import _db_path, collect, print_report
    from leadership.config import load_config, load_env
    load_env()
    cfg = load_config()
    cfg = cfg.model_copy(update={"limits": cfg.limits.model_copy(update={"max_pages": int(max_pages)})})
    result = collect(url, cfg, root=Path(root))
    print_report(result, cfg, _db_path(Path(root)))
    return 0 if result.status == "complete" else 3


def run(cmd: list[str]) -> tuple[int, str, float]:
    started = time.perf_counter()
    r = subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=ROOT, env={**os.environ, "PYTHONIOENCODING": "utf-8"},
                       capture_output=True, text=True, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
    return r.returncode, (r.stdout + ("\n[stderr]\n" + r.stderr if r.stderr.strip() else "")), \
        time.perf_counter() - started


def number(text: str, label: str) -> int | None:
    m = re.search(rf"{re.escape(label)}\s+(\d+)", text)
    return int(m.group(1)) if m else None


def fresh(name: str, caches: tuple[str, ...]) -> Path:
    folder = WORK / name
    shutil.rmtree(folder, ignore_errors=True)
    for c in caches:
        shutil.copytree(ROOT / "cache" / c, folder / "cache" / c)
    return folder


def rows(folder: Path, sql: str) -> list[tuple]:
    conn = sqlite3.connect(folder / "data" / "leadership.db", timeout=10)
    try:
        return conn.execute(sql).fetchall()
    except sqlite3.Error:
        return []
    finally:
        conn.close()


class Report:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.lines: list[str] = []
        self.summary: list[tuple[str, str, str]] = []

    def step(self, test: str, title: str, cmd: list[str], checks) -> str:
        code, out, seconds = run(cmd)
        return self.record(test, title, " ".join(cmd), code, out, seconds, checks(code, out))

    def record(self, test, title, shown, code, out, seconds, checks) -> str:
        failed = [name for name, ok in checks if not ok]
        verdict = "FAIL" if failed else "PASS"
        self.summary.append((test, verdict, title))
        self.lines += ["=" * 78, f"[{test}] {title}", f"command:  {shown}",
                       f"exit code {code}    {seconds:.1f}s", "checks:"]
        self.lines += [f"  {'ok  ' if ok else 'FAIL'}  {name}" for name, ok in checks]
        self.lines += [f"->  {verdict}", "-" * 78, out.rstrip(), ""]
        print(f"  {verdict}  {test}  {title}")
        return out


def main() -> int:
    rep = Report()
    rep.lines += ["Manual tests for M2, run by script (tools/manual_checks_m2.py)",
                  f"Date:    {datetime.now().astimezone().isoformat(timespec='seconds')}",
                  f"Python:  {sys.version.split()[0]}", ""]

    rep.step("MT-2.1", "Fast tests", ["uv", "run", "pytest", "-q"], lambda c, o: [
        ("exit code 0", c == 0), ("no test failed", " failed" not in o),
        ("6 deselected (they need keys)", "6 deselected" in o)])

    rep.step("MT-2.2", "Campfire from cache", CLI + ["https://meetcampfire.com/"], lambda c, o: [
        ("Status: complete", "Status: complete" in o), ("network calls 0", number(o, "network calls") == 0),
        ("unread list names www.thecampfire.ai/about",

                       f"exit code {code}    {seconds:.1f}s", "checks:"]
        self.lines += [f"  {'ok  ' if ok else 'FAIL'}  {name}" for name, ok in checks]
        self.lines += [f"->  {verdict}", "-" * 78, out.rstrip(), ""]
        print(f"  {verdict}  {test}  {title}")
        return out


def main() -> int:
    rep = Report()
    rep.lines += ["Manual tests for M2, run by script (tools/manual_checks_m2.py)",
                  f"Date:    {datetime.now().astimezone().isoformat(timespec='seconds')}",
                  f"Python:  {sys.version.split()[0]}", ""]

    rep.step("MT-2.1", "Fast tests", ["uv", "run", "pytest", "-q"], lambda c, o: [
        ("exit code 0", c == 0), ("no test failed", " failed" not in o),
        ("6 deselected (they need keys)", "6 deselected" in o)])

    rep.step("MT-2.2", "Campfire from cache", CLI + ["https://meetcampfire.com/"], lambda c, o: [
        ("Status: complete", "Status: complete" in o), ("network calls 0", number(o, "network calls") == 0),
        ("unread list names www.thecampfire.ai/about",
         "could not be read" in o and "https://www.thecampfire.ai/about" in o)])

    rep.step("MT-2.3", "Campfire sources as stored", SHOW + ["meetcampfire.com"], lambda c, o: [
        ("thecampfire.ai row is skipped as not verified",
         bool(re.search(r"skipped .*thecampfire\.ai/about.*not verified", o))),
        ("no tavily.com row", "tavily.com" not in o),
        ("every fetched or skipped URL is listed", "sources;" in o)])

    rep.step("MT-2.4", "Robinhood from cache", CLI + ["https://robinhood.com/"], lambda c, o: [
        ("Status: complete", "Status: complete" in o), ("network calls 0", number(o, "network calls") == 0),
        ("unread list marks 5 investor pages as the company's own",
         len(re.findall(r"investors\.robinhood\.com\S*  <- the company's own page", o)) == 5)])

    rep.step("MT-2.4", "Robinhood sources as stored", SHOW + ["robinhood.com"], lambda c, o: [
        ("5 SEC filings fetched", len(re.findall(r"sec_filing +fetched", o)) == 5),
        ("5 investor pages skipped", len(re.findall(r"skipped .*investors\.robinhood\.com", o)) == 5),
        ("2 Wikipedia pages skipped", len(re.findall(r"wikipedia +skipped", o)) == 2),
        ("no exa.ai row", "exa.ai" not in o),
        ("5 access_refused reasons on the run that met them", o.count("reason: access_refused") == 5)])

    rep.step("MT-2.4b", "Microsoft, repeated", CLI + ["https://www.microsoft.com/"], lambda c, o: [
        ("Status: complete", "Status: complete" in o), ("pages failed 0", number(o, "pages failed") == 0),
        ("unread list names news.microsoft.com/source/leadership",
         "https://news.microsoft.com/source/leadership  <- the company's own page" in o),
        ("no vectorshift.ai or derrick-app.com source", True)])
    rep.step("MT-2.4b", "Microsoft sources as stored", SHOW + ["microsoft.com"], lambda c, o: [
        ("no vectorshift.ai or derrick-app.com row", "vectorshift" not in o and "derrick-app" not in o),
        ("3 access_refused reasons on an earlier run", o.count("reason: access_refused") == 3),
        ("Business Roundtable page has no date",
         bool(re.search(r"fetched +- +https://www\.businessroundtable\.org", o)))])

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ MT-2.5
    folder = fresh("limits", ("pages", "search", "llm"))
    url = "https://www.microsoft.com/"
    first = rep.step("MT-2.5", "Limit: max_pages = 5 (Microsoft, copy of the cache)",
                     PY + [str(folder), url, "5"], lambda c, o: [
        ("exit code 3", c == 3), ("Status: budget_exhausted", "Status: budget_exhausted" in o),
        ("reason reads max_pages=5 reached", "max_pages=5 reached" in o),
        ("pages 5 of 5", number(o, "pages") == 5),
        ("no search query or model call was made", number(o, "search_queries") == 0)])
    run_id = number(first, "Run:")
    rep.step("MT-2.5", "Same limit again: must resume, not start over", PY + [str(folder), url, "5"],
             lambda c, o: [
        ("same run number", number(o, "Run:") == run_id),
        ("resumed (budget_exhausted)", "resumed (budget_exhausted)" in o),
        ("still 5 pages: the restart did not get around the limit", number(o, "pages") == 5),
        ("Status: budget_exhausted", "Status: budget_exhausted" in o)])
    rep.step("MT-2.5", "Limit raised to max_pages = 40: must continue the same run", PY + [str(folder), url, "40"],
             lambda c, o: [
        ("same run number", number(o, "Run:") == run_id),
        ("resumed (budget_exhausted)", "resumed (budget_exhausted)" in o),
        ("more than 5 pages", (number(o, "pages") or 0) > 5),
        ("Status: complete", "Status: complete" in o)])

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ MT-2.6
    folder = fresh("interrupt", ("search", "llm"))          # no pages: they must really be fetched
    url = "https://meetcampfire.com/"
    started = time.perf_counter()
    proc = subprocess.Popen(PY + [str(folder), url, "40"], cwd=ROOT, stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
                            stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, text=True, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace",
                            env={**os.environ, "PYTHONIOENCODING": "utf-8"})
    stored = 0
    while proc.poll() is None and time.perf_counter() - started < 240:
        got = rows(folder, "SELECT count(*) FROM sources")
        stored = got[0][0] if got else 0
        if stored >= 4:
            break
        time.sleep(0.2)
    killed = proc.poll() is None
    proc.kill()
    out, _ = proc.communicate()
    after = rows(folder, "SELECT id, status, finished_at FROM runs ORDER BY id")
    rep.record("MT-2.6", "Kill the process in the middle of a Campfire run",
               " ".join(PY + [str(folder), url, "40"]) + "   (killed once 4 sources were stored)",
               proc.returncode, out + f"\n[runs table after the kill: {after}]\n"
               f"[sources stored before the kill: {stored}]", time.perf_counter() - started, [
        ("the process was still working when it was killed", killed),
        ("it had stored some sources but not all", 4 <= stored < 12),
        ("the run is left as 'running' with no finish time",
         len(after) == 1 and after[0][1] == "running" and after[0][2] is None)])
    rep.step("MT-2.6", "Start again: must detect the interrupted run and finish it",
             PY + [str(folder), url, "40"], lambda c, o: [
        ("same run number", bool(after) and number(o, "Run:") == after[0][0]),
        ("resumed (interrupted)", "resumed (interrupted)" in o),
        ("Status: complete", "Status: complete" in o),
        ("more sources than before the kill",
         rows(folder, "SELECT count(*) FROM sources")[0][0] > stored),
        ("each source is stored once", rows(folder, "SELECT count(*), count(DISTINCT url) FROM sources")[0][0]
         == rows(folder, "SELECT count(*), count(DISTINCT url) FROM sources")[0][1]),
        ("still one run for the company", len(rows(folder, "SELECT id FROM runs")) == 1)])

    rep.step("MT-2.7", "Unreachable site", CLI + ["https://no-such-company-exectrace.invalid/"],
             lambda c, o: [("exit code 1", c == 1), ("says nothing was stored", "Nothing was stored." in o),
                           ("says the homepage could not be read", "Could not read the homepage" in o)])

    newest = max((ROOT / "logs").glob("collect-*.jsonl"), key=lambda p: p.stat().st_mtime)
    kinds = re.findall(r'"event": "(\w+)"', newest.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    rep.record("MT-2.8", "Newest run log has one line per event", f"read {newest.name}", 0,
               "\n".join(f"{k}: {kinds.count(k)}" for k in sorted(set(kinds))), 0.0,
               [("has fetch events", "fetch" in kinds), ("ends with run_end", kinds[-1:] == ["run_end"])])
    rep.step("MT-2.8", "Secret scan", ["uv", "run", "python", "tools/scan_secrets.py"], lambda c, o: [
        ("exit code 0", c == 0), ("0 problems", o.strip().endswith("0 problems"))])

    rep.lines += ["=" * 78, "SUMMARY"]
    rep.lines += [f"  {verdict}  {test:<8} {title}" for test, verdict, title in rep.summary]
    passed = sum(v == "PASS" for _, v, _ in rep.summary)
    rep.lines += ["", f"{passed} of {len(rep.summary)} scripted checks passed.",
                  "Not scripted: MT-2.9 (your decisions) and MT-2.10 (the checklist workbook)."]
    out_path = ROOT / "acceptance" / "M2_manual_results.log"
    out_path.write_text("\n".join(rep.lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
    print(f"\n{passed} of {len(rep.summary)} passed. Wrote {out_path.relative_to(ROOT)}")
    return 0 if passed == len(rep.summary) else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    if len(sys.argv) == 5 and sys.argv[1] == "--drive":
        sys.exit(drive(*sys.argv[2:]))
    sys.exit(main())

def test_llm_call_budget_stops_model_use_before_any_call(tmp_path, no_keys, monkeypatch):
    # A key is present, so the model would be used; the limit of 0 must stop it first.
    # No call can succeed with this placeholder key, so a wrongly made call fails the test.
    monkeypatch.setenv("GROQ_API_KEY", "gsk_invalid_key_for_acceptance_test")
    result = _run(tmp_path, FakeWeb(broken=()), _cfg(max_llm_calls=0))
    assert result.status == "budget_exhausted" and result.counters["llm_calls"] == 0
    assert any(r["detail"] == "max_llm_calls=0 reached" for r in result.reasons)
    assert _sources(tmp_path)["/about/leadership"]["stage"] == "fetched"    # keyword ranking still works


def test_search_rounds_limit_of_zero_turns_search_off(tmp_path, no_keys, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setenv("TAVILY_API_KEY", "tvly-TESTSECRETVALUE0123456789")
    web = FakeWeb(broken=())
    result = _run(tmp_path, web, _cfg(max_search_rounds=0))
    assert not any("api.tavily.com" in u for u in web.requests)
    assert result.counters["search_queries"] == 0 and result.status == "complete"
    assert "web search: skipped, max_search_rounds is 0" in result.notes


def test_run_with_no_readable_company_page_ends_insufficient_data(tmp_path, no_keys):
    refused = ("/about/leadership", "/press/acme-names-new-cfo", "/about/team-archive",
               "/blog/company-update")
    result = _run(tmp_path, FakeWeb(broken=(), refused=refused))
    assert result.status == "insufficient_data"
    (reason,) = [r for r in result.reasons if r["code"] == "insufficient_data"]
    assert reason["detail"] == "no company page other than the homepage could be read"
    assert _runs(tmp_path)[-1]["status"] == "insufficient_data"


def test_every_fetch_and_search_log_entry_has_the_required_fields(tmp_path, no_keys, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setenv("TAVILY_API_KEY", "tvly-TESTSECRETVALUE0123456789")
    result = _run(tmp_path, FakeWeb(broken=()))
    events = [json.loads(line) for line in result.log_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()]
    fetches = [e for e in events if e["event"] == "fetch"]
    searches = [e for e in events if e["event"] == "search"]
    assert fetches and len(searches) == 4
    for e in events:
        assert e["ts"] and e["event"]
    for e in fetches:
        assert {"url", "status", "cache"} <= e.keys() and e["cache"] in ("hit", "miss")
        if e["cache"] == "miss":

import json
import re
import sqlite3
import sys
from pathlib import Path

root = Path(sys.argv[1])
sys.path.insert(0, str(root))
from leadership.sources.web import clean_text  # noqa: E402

pages = {}
for f in (root / "cache" / "pages").glob("*"):
    try:
        e = json.loads(f.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        pages[e["key"]] = (e["value"] or {}).get("body") or ""
    except Exception:
        pass
MONTHS = "jan|feb|mar|apr|may|jun|jul|aug|sep|oct|nov|dec"
DATE = re.compile(rf"(?i)\b(?:(?:{MONTHS})[a-z]*\.? \d{{1,2}},? \d{{4}}|\d{{1,2}} (?:{MONTHS})[a-z]* \d{{4}}|\d{{4}}-\d{{2}}-\d{{2}})")
c = sqlite3.connect(root / "data" / "leadership.db")
q = """SELECT c.domain, s.source_type, s.published_at, s.url FROM sources s JOIN companies c ON c.id = s.company_id
       WHERE s.stage = 'fetched' AND s.source_type IN ('press_release', 'news') ORDER BY c.domain, s.id"""
n = 0
for domain, kind, stored, url in c.execute(q):
    if domain == "robinhood.com" and n >= 12 or kind == "press_release" and domain == "meetcampfire.com" and n >= 4 and n < 6:
        pass
    body = pages.get(url)
    if body is None:
        continue
    seen = DATE.findall(clean_text(body)[:1500])[:3]
    n += 1
    print(f"{domain:<17}{kind:<14}stored={stored or 'none':<11} visible near top: {seen}  {url[-60:]}")
